LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. away.headline: Seattle Seahawks Terminate Contract of Former 1,000-Yard RB
away.blurb: At 25 years old (5-foot-10, 203 pounds), he remains available for other clubs seeking running-back depth as the 2026 season continues. Eagles rule Jalen Hurts out for season amid blood clot issues Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing The Seattle Seahawks released running back Dontae McMillan from their practice squad on Monday as part of corresponding moves that also brought in tight end Josiah Deguara and fullback Jackson Acker while releasing wide receiver Malick Meiga, via the NFL transaction wire . McMillan’s brief tenure with his hometown team ended after roughly two weeks. The Seahawks signed the undrafted rookie to the practice squad on October 6 after a planned addition of veteran Joe Mixon fell through when Mixon failed a physical. The move came amid injuries in the backfield, including first-round pick Jadarian Price on injured reserve and practice-squad back Jacardia Wright also sidelined. A Seattle native and Chief Sealth High School graduate, McMillan described the signing as a dream come true. He had trained locally with former Seahawk Myles Gaskin after the Baltimore Ravens released him following training camp and preseason. In the Ravens’ preseason he rushed for 109 yards on 15 carries, including a 63-yard run. McMillan’s college production made him an appealing depth option. After beginning his career at Weber State—where he was teammates with Seahawks receiver Rashid Shaheed—he transferred to Eastern Michigan. In his final season there in 2025, he rushed for 1,014 yards and four touchdowns on 177 carries while adding 33 receptions for 375 yards and three scores. He became one of only 12 players in Eastern Michigan history to reach 1,000 rushing yards in a season and earned All-MAC Second-Team honors. Despite the strong college résumé and productive preseason showing, McMillan was not elevated to the active roster during his time in Seattle. The Seahawks’ running-back group includes players such as Emanuel Wilson, George Holani, Robert Henry Jr., and Velus Jones Jr. on the 53-man roster, with Zach Charbonnet working his way back from the physically unable to perform list. Monday’s practice-squad adjustments suggest the team is refining its depth chart as the season progresses. For McMillan, the release returns him to free agency after a short but meaningful homecoming. His path from West Seattle standout to undrafted free agent and brief Seahawks practice-squad member underscores the unpredictable nature of NFL roster decisions. home.blurb: The Seahawks have ruled out three players for Thursday night, including running back Zach Charbonnet (knee) and linebackers Chazz Surratt (calf) and Drake Thomas (ankle). Charbonnet was limited in practice throughout the week before being ruled out, leaving Seattle without one of its backfield options. Surratt and Thomas did not practice all week, leaving the Seahawks shorthanded at linebacker. Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was limited Monday and Tuesday before returning to full participation Wednesday. He carries no game designation and is expected to play. Quarterback Drew Lock (right forearm) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (ankle) were limited throughout the week but also carry no game designations. Denver will be without two key defensive starters Thursday night, with cornerback Patrick Surtain (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) both ruled out. Cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) is also questionable after being limited throughout the week, creating additional uncertainty in Denver's defensive backfield. Denver's secondary injuries are particularly concerning against a Seattle passing offense that will have Jaxon Smith-Njigba available. The Broncos have the healthier offense, but the absence of Surtain and Hufanga, along with Moss' questionable designation, gives Seattle a potential matchup advantage through the air. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Everything you need to know to catch a key AFC South game in London Getty Images The Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars are across the pond today. The Jags are playing their second consecutive international games, both taking place in London. They defeated the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week. The last-second win put them at 4-1 on the season, tied for the second-best record in the AFC. The Texans come in with a bit different standing, sitting at 1-4, though, like the Jags, they are also coming off a win. Houston got their first win against the Tennessee Titans , who now sit at 0-5. Texans vs. Jaguars need to know Jaguars London history: The Jags are pretty much London's home team, playing there at least once a year since 2013, with the exception of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an 8-7 record across the pond. Their first-ever game in England was in 2013, a loss to the 49ers at Wembley Stadium. Their first international win was their third of the kind, a 2015 game against the Bills . And of course, their most recent win came in Week 5 against the Eagles. Marvin Harrison Jr. : The biggest news out of Houston is the addition of former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. Harrison's time with the Arizona Cardinals didn't work out as expected, but he and the Texans are hoping a fresh start will be reflected in his stat line. What should help the WR make a quick adjustment to his new team is the reunion with quarterback C.J. Stroud , who he had great success with at Ohio State. Harrison will be one to watch this week as the Texans offense has the tall task of keeping up with a solid Jaguars offense. Stroud has played well despite their record, so adding Harrison could be huge for the Texans' offense. Jaguars o-line vs. Texans defense: The Jags will be without left tackle Anton Harrison , who needs surgery. The offensive line will be going up against defensive end Will Anderson Jr. , who has 27 total tackles, 7.5 sacks, a league high, and one forced fumble and recovery this season. The Jags need to protect Trevor Lawrence, especially so he can continue to improve in his game-time decisions. The Jaguars struggled a bit against the Eagles, so they will need to shake that off and go back to how they looked at the start of the season. National Media Picks Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Texans Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Texans John Pluym: Jaguars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Texans Eric Moody: Jaguars Seth Walder: Texans Jeremy Bergman: Texans Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Texans Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars Zach Berman: Texans Jon Greenberg: Texans Larry Holder: Jaguars Chad Graff: Texans Josh Kendall: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Steven Louis Goldstein: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis Jaguars get the nod over Houston 14-9, making this their second-tightest voting split this year after their Week 2 game against the Denver Broncos. This is not exactly surprising considering the Jaguars and Texans played each other so tightly two years ago, and considering the fact that so many had picked the Texans to win the AFC South to begin with. Houston just needed one win against the hapless Titans to draw closer to the Jaguars in terms of votes. I think this will be a close game because, on paper, these two teams are close in nearly every area. The Jaguars have a much better running game than the Texans do, but both teams have talented quarterbacks who are playing well, proven head coaches, explosive pass-catchers, strong defenses, so on and so forth. Even the biggest question for each team is the same (the offensive lines). While the Texans are 1-4, everything indicates this is a closer matchup on paper than one would think just looking at the records. With that said, I think the fact the Jaguars have been a more complete team this season is no accident and is not owrth simply tossing aside. The Jaguars have been one of the best teams in the NFL this season, and the Jaguars have more things to hang their hat on right now than this Texans squad does. I have the Jaguars 27, Texans 24 in what should be another one-score game that gets decided with a late score or stop. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect David Montgomery, Jalen Pitre Out as Expected David Montgomery, Jalen Pitre Out as Expected Two of the non-participants from the Texans' Wednesday practice were to be expected: that's running back David Montgomery, who's dealing with a groin injury, as well as defensive back Jalen Pitre, who suffered an AC joint sprain during last weekend's game against the Tennessee Titans. As of now, their status is considered week-to-week, meaning there's a good chance that both could be sidelined for Week 6 against the Jaguars, yet might not have to be forced on injured reserve, which would take them out for a minimum of four weeks. The two other DNPs from the Texans' practice— linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair and Trent Brown— have both been dealing with some nagging injuries through the past couple of weeks that effectively left them to sit out of Wednesday's practice. However, considering both played in last week's game against the Titans while dealing with their respective injuries, it'd be fair to assume that both are still on track to play in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Henry To'oTo'o Trending Up for Return The Texans officially activated the 21-day return window for Henry To'oTo'o on Wednesday, who's been sidelined for the past four weeks due to a shoulder injury he suffered in Week 1 against the Buffalo Bills. A limited participation in practice is a great sign that his return is right around the corner. However, he might still be ruled inactive for Week 6 against the Jaguars if unable to complete a full practice. If that's the case, Jake Hansen will remain Houston's fill in as their WLB. Another aspect of the Texans' injury report that can't go unnoticed: wide receiver Tank Dell has participated in his first full practice since being designated to return from his knee injury suffered back in 2024. That means, if all goes smoothly over the coming days, there's a chance that Dell could make his long-awaited return to the lineup in Week 6. But until the Texans officially activate him from injured reserve , we won't know for sure about when he'll officially be good to be elevated on the gameday roster. home.blurb: If Al-Shaair is out for the rest of the game, the Texans will likely turn to Jake Hansen as the next linebacker. He's started the past three games in place of the injured Henry To'oTo'o, who returned from the injured reserve ahead of Week 6's matchup. This is not for the Texans ' defense entering the closing minutes of the second quarter. Following the touchdown run from Jacksonville, Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was down on the ground and needed to be looked at by trainers. According to the broadcast, Al-Shaair already wasn't feeling well going into the game and needed to eat a banana before the last drive. Keep in mind this is Al-Shaair's second game back since dealing with the groin injury suffered in Week 3's loss to the Colts . According to the injury report, he's being evaluated for a concussion. Al-Shaair, who led the Texans in tackles over the past two years, recorded four tackles before leaving Sunday's matchup in London. The sloppy weather conditions have certainly played a factor toward the injures in Week 6 away from Reliant Stadium. The Texans will begin the second half on offense. home.blurb: Montaric Brown missed Wednesday's practice with a lingering hamstring issue—the same injury that sidelined him against Cincinnati and limited him to just six snaps last week. If Brown isn't cleared for Sunday, the Jaguars have no choice but to throw Travis Hunter out there for every single defensive snap, like the last two weeks. He logged 76 snaps against the Bengals and stayed on the field for all 62 defensive reps against the Eagles—plus six snaps on offense. Asking a two-way talent to anchor the secondary full-time week in and week out is playing with fire. It simply isn't a sustainable game plan, leaving him dangerously exposed to wear and tear. What's worse, there is virtually no safety net behind Hunter. With Christian Braswell out and Jourdan Lewis playing through his own ailments, the Jaguars are essentially one injury away from putting practice squad guys on the boundary against C.J. Stroud . Safety Eric Murray (concussion), right tackle Cole Van Lanen (knee), left guard Emmanuel Pregnon (toe), cornerback Jourdan Lewis (hamstring), cornerback Jaylon Jones (hamstring), cornerback Jarrian Jones (elbow), and rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher (back) did get some work Wednesday, but remained limited in practice. Atlanta will look to earn its first home victory of the season against a Chicago team featuring quarterback Caleb Williams and the NFL’s No. 1 rushing offense. The Falcons On SI staff is unanimous in its prediction. Falcons SI staff each enter the week with a 3-2 record on the season. Here is what each writer predicts for Sunday’s matchup. Gerald Thomas, III (3-2) Atlanta took a tough blow in its overtime loss to the Ravens last week. It was a reality check for sure, but also gave the Falcons direction of where to improve. The Falcons win by stopping the Bears’ No. 1 rushing offense , led by D’Andre Swift. They will catch a break with the second head of the backfield monster, Kyle Monangai, being ruled out for his second straight game with turf toe and a thumb injury. Stop the run and get pressure on a returning-from-injury Caleb Williams, and Atlanta secures its first win at home for the year. Prediction : Falcons 35, Bears 24 Scott Kennedy (3-2) Michael Penix Jr. has been one of the best quarterbacks this season when he’s not pressured. The Bears haven’t been pressuring quarterbacks and are missing edge rusher Montez Sweat. Penix keeps the defense honest with his arm, while Bijan Robinson does Bijan Robinson things. The defense contains the Bears No.1 rushing offense, but Caleb Williams has a big game on broken plays. Falcons do enough to even their record. Prediction : Falcons 27, Bears 22 Darius Hayes (3-2) Caleb Williams’ return adds another layer to Sunday’s matchup as the Falcons look to respond after a tough overtime loss to the Ravens. Atlanta’s biggest challenge will be slowing down Chicago’s No. 1 ranked rushing offense after struggling to contain Baltimore on the ground last week. I expect the Falcons to deliver a stronger defensive performance while getting their offense back on track. Atlanta should do enough on both sides of the ball to secure a hard fought victory, earn its first home win of the season and improve to 3-3. Prediction : Falcons 31, Bears 23 Garrett Chapman (3-2): The health of the two quarterbacks, Michael Penix Jr. (ribs) and Caleb Williams (hamstring), will ultimately dictate how this game goes. Both are set to play, but how healthy will they be? The Bears have shown some outrageous scoring spurts (59 points in Week 1), but it's been a rocky road since then because of various injuries. Atlanta's defensive line will need another big performance on Sunday. Both secondaries have shown they can be exploited this season, but Penix needs to stay clean. If he can, the Falcons quarterback has been one of the best quarterbacks when not under pressure. The Bears have some pass rushers who are set to miss this game , so that could be the formula for a Falcons win. Prediction : Falcons 24, Bears 20 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-2) As long as Penix is healthy (and plays like it), the Falcons offense is going to be tough for the Bears to match up against. The Bears are without their best defensive lineman, Montez Sweat, and honestly, their d-line is pretty bad even when he's healthy. The Bears' top corner, Jaylon Johnson, is having a bad start to the year, so I look for Drake London to have yet another big game. While Caleb Williams' return is the big headline, the biggest test for the Falcons' defense will be whether they can contain the Bears' rushing attack. The Falcons' run defense got gashed by an elite Ravens rushing attack, and now they'll face a Bears rushing attack that's just as good. Ultimately though, I trust the Falcons defense and Jeff Ulbrich to get some stops when they need them. Prediction : Falcons 27, Bears 23 The game kicks off at 1 p.m. at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on FOX . away.blurb: It is apparent that Swift very well could still be dealing with these injuries, but they haven't kept him out of practice. The Bears have been careful with Swift because there is absolutely no possible way he's been fully healthy. But, he's been "healthy enough" to roll out there on game days. Bears Week 5 inactives: Caleb Williams officially ruled out against Packers Over the last two games, we have seen a dramatic decrease in overall rushing performance from the Chicago Bears. Now, the elephant in the room here is the fact that Kyle Monangai has missed these games. Monangai is vital to this Bears league-leading rushing attack, and the offense has missed him greatly. D'Andre Swift, on the other hand, hasn't been on the injury report and, by all front-facing accounts, is healthy. A recent D'Andre Swift trend should have Bears fans questioning his health If you look a little further into the ground game, you'll notice something alarming: Swift has a total of five second-half carries over the last two games. Five total . In the second half against the Green Bay Packers in Week 5, Swift was given only one carry that went for eight yards. Then, against the Falcons in Week 6, he had just four carries. When speaking on the subject, offensive coordinator Press Taylor admitted that Swift's second-half usage has been largely due to wanting to preserve him for the full length of the season. And, while that makes sense, I still don't think it's telling the whole story. Leading up to the Green Bay game, Swift was dealing with knee and hip injuries. But, he played in that game and the following week in Atlanta. In the two games he's had since dealing with those injuries, though, do we think it's any coincidence that he's essentially been shelved in the second half? Go back and watch him run these past two weeks and you'll notice that he doesn't look quite like himself, either. He isn't as shifty and has not run with as much explosion or aggression. The Bears cannot possibly be "riding the hot hand" at times with Roschon Johnson. He's looked like anything but the hot hand for the vast majority of his touches this season. Outside of maybe three or four plays, in fact, Johnson has had me going full-on Wolverine laying in bed gripping a photo of Kyle Monangai. The Bears can't get Kyle Monangai back soon enough And I think that's where this story leads: all the way back to Monangai. Still, with Monangai actually missing time, Chicago knows it cannot force the issue with Swift, thus risking being down both of their top two running backs. God forbid we have to suffer through an entire game of Roschon Johnson and whatever reserve running back Ben Johnson pairs him up with. Right now, this Bears offense is basically surviving when it comes to the ground game. Swift has not been himself. Roschon is less than ideal and only a Band-Aid at this point. away.headline: Bears Friday injury report: Will Caleb Williams play vs. Falcons?
away.blurb: The Bears conducted their final practice of the week, which included final game designations for Sunday. Quarterback Caleb Williams practiced in full for a third straight day, an indication that he's poised to return to the lineup in Week 6. But Williams, who's missed the last three games, is questionable. There are some last step hurdles for him to clear, but all indications are he will be under center vs. the Falcons. Elsewhere, cornerback Kyler Gordon was also a full participant in practice all week, and he's questionable for Sunday's game as he looks to return from the PUP list. The Bears have also ruled out four players: linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring), running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) and linebacker Keyshaun Elliott (quad). The Chicago Bears are gearing up for their Week 6 game against the Atlanta Falcons, where Chicago is looking to get back on track after a brutal Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers . away.blurb: After a disastrous Week 5, the optimism surrounding Chicago took a hit, as did its standing in the national power rankings. Despite having a strong coaching staff and roster, the Bears showed just how much Williams means to the team. His impact under center and the way his return energized his teammates were on full display in Chicago’s 31-23 win. Now, the Bears have an opportunity to make another statement on Thursday night. “Caleb Williams was stellar in his return to the offense, opening up everything that was trapped behind padlocks in Green Bay. With the Iceman at the controls, everyone ate: Colston Loveland caught a touchdown pass, D’Andre Swift scored twice, Roschon Johnson bullied his way into the end zone, and the Bears could not be denied. That said, they need to clean up their penalties (12 for 133 yards on Sunday) and finish games more comfortably than they did in Atlanta.” — Nick Shook (NFL.com) “The 31-23 win over the Falcons wasn’t really that close. The Bears let down in the fourth quarter, turning a 31-7 lead into a one-score game. That’s not ideal but the way they played through three quarters in Caleb Williams’ return was impressive. Cornerback Kyler Gordon’s odd 2026 took a positive turn. Gordon had missed the offseason and the first five games due to a calf injury, prompting questions about his future with the team. In just 17 snaps on Sunday, Gordon had three sacks and two forced fumbles. He’s the first Bears defensive back with three sacks in a game since Todd Bell in 1983. He’s just the second defensive back in NFL history with three sacks and two forced fumbles in a game, joining Rod Kush of the Houston Oilers in 1985, according to the Bears’ site. His playmaking will be welcomed on the Bears’ defense.” — Frank Schwab (Yahoo Sports) Williams’ Return Sends Bears Back Into the Top 10 Williams’ return has already lifted Chicago in the national power rankings. After beating the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, Chicago faces a short turnaround before hosting the New England Patriots on Thursday night . The primetime matchup will feature two of the top three picks from the 2024 NFL Draft as Caleb Williams and Drake Maye lead their respective offenses in a battle between two young quarterbacks looking to establish themselves among the league’s best. The Bears and Patriots have a history of notable matchups, but the franchises rarely meet, with just 16 official meetings all-time. New England enters this matchup as the defending AFC champion, while Chicago is looking to build on its Week 6 victory and establish momentum as the season progresses. With both teams eyeing another step forward, Thursday night’s contest offers an intriguing test for the Bears against a New England team that has started the season well. The Bears will need to maintain disciplined rush lanes, limit his scrambling opportunities, and prevent him from turning broken plays into explosive gains. New England’s offensive success will also depend on its ability to establish balance and protect Maye. The Patriots will look to use their running game to keep Chicago’s defense honest while creating opportunities for Maye to attack through the air. For the Bears, generating consistent pressure without sacrificing coverage discipline will be critical. Chicago must also limit yards after the catch and prevent New England from sustaining long drives. If the Bears can force the Patriots into predictable passing situations, they will have more opportunities to disrupt Maye and create turnovers. The Patriots’ defense will present another important challenge for Chicago, particularly as Williams continues to develop in his second NFL season. home.headline: Bears report card: How we graded Chicago in Week 6 win vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Chicago’s defense was outstanding in this game. However, after giving up just one measly touchdown in the first three quarters, they started to unravel a bit in the fourth after their starters were pulled up 31-7. The positive side of the B comes from how well they played, but it’s not an A because of the door cracking open for Atlanta in the final frame. Kyler Gordon made his return from injury, which made this his season debut. It seemed like there was some off-the-field drama with his absence, but like most of these types of stories, they’re overblown. He looked ready to go in a big way once he stepped on the field. In addition to making four tackles, Gordon had three sacks and two forced fumbles. He could play this well again in every game and still not have stats like that. It’s looking like a big boost to their group going forward. Chicago’s defense needed a spark in the defensive backfield and with their pass rush. They didn’t expect Kyler Gordon to give them help in both areas, but that was the case in Atlanta. With the two teams that won their respective conferences last season up next, the Bears knew that getting a win in Atlanta was important. Getting to 4-2 made it so they could battle the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks with a bit more confidence. The Bears are becoming known as an offensive team, but the defense has left a lot to be desired. In this win on Sunday, everybody did enough to make sure they got on the flight home with the win. Here's how we graded every unit after the Week 6 victory. The Bears offense scored 31 points. Caleb Williams retur4ned from an injury and dominated as well as he ever has in the NFL. He completed 30-of-36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. Colston Loveland caught the lone touchdown pass, and it was his best overall game because of his six total catches on seven targets. Luther Burden caught all eight of his receptions for a total of 95 yards. Outside of those two, the ball was equally spread around. If Williams thinks you can help advance the ball, he’ll throw it to you. In the run game, without Kyle Monangai, the Bears did just enough with D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson. Between them, they had three rushing touchdowns, which played key roles in the win. The Bears special teams units were incredible in this game. Cairo Santos missed a 56-yard field goal, but they probably shouldn’t have put him in that position anyway. He was nails on every other attempt. They had plenty of good field position thanks to returns by Zavion Thomas and Kalif Raymond, but their punting unit also made some noise. Between causing two turnovers and pinning the Falcons deep, they did a great job. This is one of the rare special teams A-grades for doing more than just “not messing things up”. The offense and the defense had things easier on Sunday thanks to special teams. The Bears coaching staff came very close to getting an A. Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. DraftKings Sportsbook has the Ravens as 5.5-point favorites, a full one-point change from where the spread was on Tuesday morning . Still, Jackson didn't practice on Wednesday, which makes his status for Sunday a little murky. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that the two-time league MVP is "day-to-day." Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. The Baltimore Ravens are no strangers to playing without their star quarterback, and that helps to explain why they're 3-point favorites on Sunday despite backup Tyler Huntley starting. My Ravens vs. Browns predictions back Baltimore to grind out a win while leaning on Derrick Henry, who can exploit a vulnerable Cleveland run defense. Here are my NFL picks ahead of this Sunday, Oct. 18, clash, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET today. Ravens vs Browns prediction today: Ravens -3.5 The Baltimore Ravens are chasing their fourth straight win over the Cleveland Browns , and Lamar Jackson's absence isn't deterring me from fading a Cleveland team that crashed back to earth last weekend. Even with Todd Monken's knowledge of his former team, I'll lay the points - playable anywhere from -3 to -4. Tyler Huntley , one of the NFL's better backup QBs, led Baltimore to an overtime win in Week 5, and he's now 3-0 as a starter since last season. But this pick is more about what Derrick Henry can do against a Browns defense that's allowing 117.4 rushing yards per game and could be without Carson Schwesinger and Mason Graham (both questionable). On the other side of the ball, look for the visitors to be opportunistic against Deshaun Watson , who was sacked eight times in Week 5 and may have to do more in the passing game given the hosts' backfield injuries. The Ravens are 4-2 ATS in their past six road games , and two of the last three meetings between these teams have been emphatic Baltimore blowouts. TOP PICK Ravens vs Browns player prop: Derrick Henry Over 88.5 rushing yards The Ravens have handed Henry a heavy workload once again this season - he leads the league with 113 carries while averaging 95.2 YPG on the ground, and yet there's room for more with Jackson sidelined. This AFC North duel is a favorable matchup for King Henry, too, with the Browns giving up 134 rushing yards last weekend in New York and dealing with injuries across the defensive line . I don't see that banged-up unit being a match for Baltimore's powerhouse RB, who sits third in the NFL in yards after contact (262). Henry has gone past this O/U number in eight of his last 10 outings , and a run-heavy script should produce 20+ carries. Ravens vs Browns combo The Ravens have scored 24+ points in each of their wins this year , and this line feels too low despite Jackson being sidelined. The Over is 7-3 in Baltimore's last 10 games, and it's been a winning ticket in the past five meetings between these teams . With Cleveland sweating on the health of key defensive playmakers, Huntley can deliver a similar stat line to his SNF effort against the Falcons (201 passing yards, two TD passes, no turnovers), while the Browns' offense is boosted by KC Concepcion clearing the concussion protocol. When Baltimore isn't riding Henry and the ground game, look for Mark Andrews to be a key checkdown option for Huntley. Andrews has 22 catches through five contests, and he's finished with 6+ targets in four of those outings . Ravens moneyline Mark Andrews Over 3.5 receptions Ravens vs Browns touchdown scorer: Harold Fannin Jr. The Browns feel likelier to have success through the air than on the ground on Sunday, and Harold Fannin Jr. stands out as an anytime TD pick after grabbing three scores already this year . Baltimore has given up three touchdowns to tight ends in the opening five weeks , and snap count shouldn't be an issue for Fannin Jr. after logging a 93% mark last weekend against the Jets. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Thursday injury report for the Browns Week 6 against the Ravens
away.blurb: After an overwhelming 11 players sat out on Wednesday, several key starters on the offensive line, defensive interior, and skill positions returned to the field in a limited or full capacity. Thursday provided major relief for the depth chart as four players upgraded from Wednesday’s DNP list to limited status. Veteran defensive tackle Maliek Collins returned to practice to help steady the interior, while starting right tackle Tytus Howard got back on the field. On offense, backup running back Dylan Sampson and tight end Carsen Ryan both progressed to limited work. They join wide receivers Denzel Boston, Tylan Wallace, and KC Concepcion (concussion protocol), along with safety Grant Delpit, who all remained limited. Starting center Elgton Jenkins upgraded from limited on Wednesday to a full participant on Thursday, clearing any minor knee concern ahead of Sunday. Quarterback Dillon Gabriel maintained his full participation status as he continues to build momentum. Here is Thursday's full injury report breakdown as we progress through Week 6. away.headline: Concerning Lamar Jackson Injury Update Shifts Bengals vs. Ravens Odds in NFL Week 7
away.blurb: Concerning Lamar Jackson Injury Update Shifts Bengals vs. Ravens Odds in NFL Week 7 Skip to main content ON SI Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has not played since Week 4, and his status for Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals still remains unclear. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson could "potentially" practice this week after missing all three of the team's practices ahead of Week 6. There have been reports the last two weeks that Jackson has a chance to play through his ankle injury, but he has not suited up in practice -- or for a game -- since Week 4. Minter: Lamar Jackson (ankle) could "potentially" practice this week. Remains day-to-day. Minter's update on Jackson isn't viewed as a positive one in the betting market. Ahead of Week 7, oddsmakers set the Ravens as three-point favorites at home in their matchup with the Bengals. Now, DraftKings Sportsbook has Baltimore set as a 2.5-point favorite, though it remains -148 on the moneyline to win this game. It's not a major adjustment, but clearly there is some worry that Jackson could miss his third game in a row. Currently, DraftKings has received 73 percent of the moneyline bets in this game on the Bengals to win outright. After going down against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, Jackson has not played. He missed a win over Atlanta in Week 5 and a loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. The Cleveland loss looms large for the Ravens, as they are now behind the Browns in the AFC North standings. The Ravens are a much more dangerous team with Jackson in the lineup, and he was an MVP candidate before going down in Week 4. This season, the star quarterback has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. A two-time MVP, Jackson leads the league in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating in 2026. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score, a sign that his rushing is back to a higher level than it was in 2025. Tyler Huntley would receive the start in Week 7 if Jackson can't go. Dating back to last season, the Ravens are 3-1 in Huntley's last four starts, but they remain 7-12 all-time when Jackson is sidelined. Huntley struggled to move the offense in Week 6, throwing for 165 yards and a score in a 13-10 loss. He did combine for three scores in the win over Atlanta, so there is a higher ceiling that what he showed this past Sunday. If Jackson doesn't practice on Wednesday, it's possible this line could move even further towards the Bengals. For now, oddsmakers are still giving the Ravens the edge in this divisional battle. Trey Hendrickson Will Make His Return "We're always going to try to have the best interest of the player," Minter said. "The path that we went down was really in [Hendrickson]'s best interest, both short-term and long-term. [I'm] excited for him to be back out there." The Ravens ruled out defensive tackle Broderick Washington Jr. (ankle), who didn't practice Thursday or Friday. He has six tackles so far this season. Minter also ruled out Cam Jurgens (concussion) for Sunday's game, meaning rookie Vega Ioane will get another start at center.. The Ravens also have other offensive line injuries to monitor with guards Andrew Vorhees (foot) and Emery Jones Jr. (ankle) both questionable to play. They were limited throughout the week. Wide receivers Zay Flowers (toe) and Rashod Bateman (shoulder) are good to go with no injury designation. Flowers was limited Thursday and Friday but Bateman returned to full participation. Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane could return from injured reserve after he suffered a wrist injury in Week 1 in Indianapolis. Lane had three full days of practice this week and is listed as questionable. He would have to be removed from injured reserve this weekend to play. While the Ravens could be at full strength at receiver, they're short at tight end with rookie Matt Hibner (hand) ruled out for Sunday's game. He didn't practice this week. Per Minter, the rookie tight end is not a candidate to be placed on injured reserve. Multiple Browns Leaders Return to Practice, Questionable to Play All three were limited in Friday's practice, along with veteran defensive end Derek Barnett (ankle). The Browns ruled out defensive tackle Mike Hall (ankle), quarterback Dillon Gabriel (back), defensive tackle Kalia Davis (quad), guard Teven Jenkins (back) and running back Dylan Sampson (knee). away.headline: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Ravens QB's Status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
away.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game," with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. home.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
home.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. home.headline: Browns Get Optimistic Injury Outlook Ahead of Week 6
home.blurb: The defensive duo of Mason Graham and Carson Schwesinger both returned to the practice field for the first time this week, on Friday. They both share a questionable game status heading into the weekend, but it's certainly a step in the right direction toward both suiting up against Baltimore. Graham has been dealing with knee and ankle ailments dating back to Cleveland's Thursday night win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4. The injuries kept him out of commission for last week's loss to the New York Jets, but could be poised to make a critical return. As for Schwesinger, he was seen leaving the locker room in New York in a walking boot and has been nursing an ankle injury this week. The reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year dealt with a similar situation last season, where he didn't practice the first two days of the week, then was limited for a Friday practice and wound up playing against the Jets two days later. Joining Graham and Schwesinger as questionable is star running back Quinshon Judkins, who has also been battling an ankle injury this week. He too returned to practice on Friday after missing the previous two days. Fellow running back Dylan Sampson has also been ramping things up after an IR stint this week. Sampson was limited on Thursday and Friday, but was ruled out. DE Derek Barnett, who is dealing with an ankle injury, is also listed as questionable. Two active players were officially ruled out in DT Mike Hall Jr (ankle) and G Teven Jenkins, who has missed each of the first five weeks of the season due to a back injury. DT Kalia Davis has been ruled out, as well. He spent the first four weeks on the IR, then had his 21-day practice window opened last week, but has only practiced once since then. Similarly, Dillon Gabriel has practiced every day since returning to practice off the IR ahead of Week 5, but also won't be activated this week. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the fifth straight week in a row now, we can say that the Tennessee Titans fell short of expectations. What was initially painted as a bounce-back campaign for Robert Saleh and the franchise has turned into a recurring question from fans in Nashville: "How much longer will it take for this thing to change?" The answer? I wish I could give it to you. Instead, the Tennessee Titans stand alongside the Miami Dolphins as one of the only two teams without a win this season. On the road against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6, it no longer appears to be about things changing in the present. At this point, any sign of life on the way to a victory would do. In the split spirit of both optimism and reality, here's one reason the Titans will beat the Colts tomorrow, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction to split the difference. Will: Robert Saleh's defense bounces back Oct 11, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh walks onto the field during pre-game warmups against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a score on 26 completions. The QB also found a touchdown on the ground as Houston ran away with a 26-3 victory. If Tennessee wins this week, it will be by slowing down a hot Colts offense with a massive recovery. Shut down Jonathan Taylor in the backfield, and who knows how far this team can get. Positively, Tennessee has done a solid job stopping the run this year in large part. The Texans rushed for just 79 yards last week in total. With star WR Alec Pierce on IR and reserve Ashton Dulin also set to miss time, QB Daniel Jones' options will be relatively limited. A Titans win would be about finding spurts of offensive momentum by way of defensive playmaking. Won't: Cam Ward continues to decline The lack of that offensive momentum, however, is the exact reason why Tennessee could come up short. Second-year QB Cam Ward has failed to generate any real momentum under center this season, and his shortcomings have the Titans punching up to begin with. Against Houston, Ward took four sacks and threw an interception for the third straight game. He's thrown less than 200 yards in four of the Titans' five games (five losses) this season. His full total is now out to three scores and three interceptions. That simply won't cut it for Tennessee's needed franchise QB. Promising weapons surrounding Ward, such as Wan'Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate in the WR room, haven't been able to elevate his underwhelming run. If the Titans fall short, you can safely bet it will be due to Ward once again falling short of the bar. Prediction: Titans lose, 27-17 Much like the Titans' early-season loss to the Texans last season (in which Tennessee went scoreless), I expect a relative surge of momentum from the offense. However, I don't expect the Titans to find a road win as they did vs. the Cardinals in 2025. Indy, while coming off a loss to the Steelers, has already collected two wins and consistently scored 20+ points. Their lone contest failing that margin came against Houston, in a 19-17 victory. Daniel Jones passes twice as much as Cam Ward (hardly hyperbole), and Taylor remains one of the NFL's premier backs. I predict Tennessee will surpass their three-point showing from Week 5, and things may even appear interesting early on. Still, there's nothing of present about this Titans team to suggest that a breakthrough is on the horizon. In an AFC South-bound duel tomorrow, I unfortunately anticipate the losing streak to continue. All we can hope for is a surprise from Saleh and a squad that, up to now, haven't done near enough to spark midseason hope. picks.headline: 3 last-second predictions for Titans week 6 matchup against Colts
picks.blurb: The Tennessee Titans are eyeing their first win of the season on Sunday , as head coach Robert Saleh's squad is on the road to take on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6. 2026 hasn't treated Tennessee well at all. The Titans are 0-5 and coming off a blowout 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans at home. With kickoff at Lucas Oil Stadium on the way, let's take a look at a few last-second predictions for Tennessee's contest against the Colts. Cam Ward Doesn't Commit a Turnover It's been a rough start to the year for Ward , who was expected to take a major leap in his second season and establish himself as the Titans' quarterback of the future. The 2025 No. 1 overall pick has thrown three touchdowns and three interceptions so far this season and has also added two scores on the ground. Ward has tossed an interception in each of the last three games, but that streak should come to an end Sunday. The Colts have snagged just one interception in 2026, and are one of the worst pass defenses in the NFL, allowing the fifth-most passing yards per game (254.0). Week 6 is the perfect opportunity for Ward to get back on track and build some momentum as November nears. The Miami product still has time to prove that he is capable of being Tennessee's long-term answer at the most consequential position in the sport. Titans Defense Holds Colts Offense to Under 20 Points Despite receiving little support from their offense, the Titans' defense has quietly been a solid unit this season. Saleh's group is 11th in the NFL in points per game allowed (21.8) , and is middle of the pack in passing yards (217.8) and rushing yards (114.0) allowed per game. The Colts' offense has been dynamic at times, but they've also had their struggles, especially quarterback Daniel Jones. However, the team's star running back, Jonathan Taylor, is still one of the best in the league at his position. Taylor is top-ten in rushing yards (398) and touchdowns (6), though he has been a bit inefficient, rushing for 3.9 yards per carry. If Tennessee can limit Taylor on the ground and make Jones uncomfortable in the pocket, the Titans should be able to hold the Colts to under 20 points, increasing their chances of winning . The Titans Still Lose The Titans are currently riding a six-game losing streak against the Colts and an 11-game losing streak against AFC South opponents. Unfortunately, I have both of those skids continuing. Tennessee should keep Sunday's game close and show progress. However, the Titans haven't shown enough to prove that they can storm into enemy territory and get the job done versus a Colts team that has playoff potential. We'll see when, or if, the Titans tally a win in 2026. It likely won't be in Week 6. away.headline: Titans activate Joshua Williams from IR, remove him from injury report
away.blurb: Although he was questionable heading into the weekend, the veteran defensive back has practiced fully over the past two weeks and appears to have recovered from the pec injury that forced him to miss an extended period in training camp and landed him on the injured list; he will now be available for the divisional matchup and has no injury designation for Sunday’s contest. Out of the gate, Williams should slide into a core special teams role as he works into a secondary rotation, though with Alontae Taylor and Cor’Dale Flott struggling, he may get the chance to contribute sooner rather than later. To make room for Williams, Tennessee waived defensive back Erick Hallett from the active roster for a second time in 2026 and will likely attempt to bring him back to the practice squad if he clears waivers. away.headline: New York Jets receive mixed bag of news on injury report ahead of crucial AFC East showdown against New England Patriots
away.blurb: The Jets will be without two important offensive playmakers against New England, but the return of a promising young rookie provides some much-needed optimism. Let's start with the bad. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that two key weapons on the offense, in both running back Breece Hall, who has a quad injury, and wide receiver AD Mitchell, who has a finger injury, have been ruled out for Sunday's game against New England. That's not how it played out. Hall sat out against Chicago, missed last week's win over the Cleveland Browns , and now he's going to miss a third straight game. Look, at this point, the Jets could have put him on IR and freed up a roster spot. They haven't done that, and for whatever reason, the team keeps holding the door open for a return that hasn't come. That's been frustrating to watch. I'm high on both of these guys. Cooper gives the Jets a receiver who can take attention away from Wilson on the outside, and Sadiq is a matchup problem for linebackers and safeties. With Hall and Mitchell out, the Jets need their young talent to step up, and this is the perfect spot for both rookies to show what they can do. home.headline: NFL insiders provide injury updates for Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson, Will Campbell
home.blurb: The New England Patriots added a pair of key players to their growing list of injury concerns during their blowout win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday as running back TreVeyon Henderson and left tackle Will Campbell each exited and did not return. The team has also been shorthanded at wide receiver. Offseason acquisition A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in the team's season opener and hasn't played since, though according to multiple reports he could be nearing a return. In addition, Mack Hollins was placed on injured reserve with a calf injury he suffered against the Bills. October 13, 2026 / 2:41 PM EDT / CBS Boston On Tuesday, NFL insiders provided updates on both Henderson and Campbell's injuries. Of the pair, the news was worse for Henderson. According to Adam Schefter of ESPN , the running back suffered a high ankle sprain in the second quarter of Sunday's game and is expected to miss multiple weeks. According to Schefter, Henderson will not require surgery and the team is hoping he will be back "relatively soon." The news was slightly better for Campbell, whose right knee got rolled up on, also in the second quarter. It was the same knee that Campbell hurt last year. Last season, he was placed on injured reserve. When he returned to action, Campbell wasn't the same player for the stretch run as New England made it all the way to the Super Bowl. Following Sunday's injury, Tom Pelissero reported that Campbell avoided a major knee injury. The NFL insider reported that Campbell is considered week-to-week. Rookie first-round draft pick Caleb Lomu would likely replace Campbell at left tackle should he be forced to miss time. Lomu came in following Campbell's injury and performed well against the Raiders. The Patriots have won back-to-back games despite a growing injury list. Star cornerback Christian Gonzalez missed both games, and fellow defensive back Carlton Davis joined him as inactive against the Raiders. Head coach Mike Vrabel was asked after Sunday's game how the team has embraced the next man up mentality. "Because that's what it has to be. You know what I mean? It's, we try not to panic," Vrabel said. "We just try to get the next guy ready. We ask everybody to prepare as a starter, so credit to the football players, you know, particularly the guys on this team, uh, the guys that we've tried to bring in here. And they realize that when you get an opportunity and you do something with it, then you get more opportunities." How do the Patriots continue to overcome injuries to rack up wins?

picks.blurb: Why the Giants Will Beat the Saints, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New York Giants host a struggling New Orleans Saints team looking to snap a three-game losing streak that has drawn attention and stern words from team owner Gayle Benson this past week. The Saints have the league’s 20th-ranked offense (322.0 yards per game) and the 25th-ranked defense (361.0 yards per game) as they head into MetLife Stadium against a Giants team that has a chance to go 4-0 at home for the first time since 2008, when they got off to a 6-0 start at home. Despite the Saints’ struggles, they enter this game as a 1.5-point favorite per FanDuel , which is a head-scratcher considering they have averaged 21.3 points in their last three games, while the home team has averaged 25 points per game. But odds aside, the NFC East-leading Giants’ goal, according to head coach John Harbaugh, is simple: stack wins. “You always know what they are, but you know you’ve got to stack wins to make the December standings matter,” Harbaugh said when asked how much he pays attention to the standings at this point in the season. “So, we focus on the next game.” The Giants, according to Tankathon , have to make hay, so to speak. They face a remaining schedule with a combined winning percentage of .484, with their four toughest opponents being the 49ers, Jaguars, Lions, and Browns. All four of those challenging opponents land on the schedule after the Giants’ Week 8 bye. But to focus on what the Giants might do this week, let’s look at the best- and worst-case scenarios. Why the Giants Will Beat the Saints Oct 11, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. (29) runs the ball during the third quarter against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If there was ever a good week for the Giants’ rushing game to snap out of its funk, this would be it. The league’s 30th-ranked run defense has struggled big time this season, allowing 4.9 yards per rushing attempt. If there was ever a good week for the Giants’ rushing game to snap out of its funk, this would be it. The league’s 30th-ranked run defense has struggled big time this season, allowing 4.9 yards per rushing attempt. It also ranks last in the league in defensive rush success (52.5%), meaning it struggles to stop opponents from gaining the minimum required yardage on a run (excluding kneeldowns and scrambles). The Giants’ rushing offense has not been the same since quarterback Jaxson Dart landed on IR with a season-ending knee injury. Although it ranks 17th in total rushing yards, it also averages a dismal 3.7 yards per attempt, 24th in the league. As if the rushing game’s struggles aren’t enough, it will be interesting to see if Harbaugh decides to reduce running back Cam Skattebo’s touches this week given his fumbling issue. As usual, the head coach was mum on the plans, but this could be a week when Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy Jr. get bigger roles in the rushing attack to see if they can jumpstart it. On the defensive side, the Giants’ pass rush has finally awakened after a slow start, recording seven sacks over the last two weeks. This week, they face a Saints offensive line that has surrendered three sacks to quarterback Tyler Shough over that same period. Combine that with the opportunistic Giants secondary, which has forced eight turnovers this season , against a Saints offense that has committed 13 giveaways, and the Giants’ quest to remain undefeated at home could get a lot easier. Why the Giants Won’t Beat the Saints Oct 5, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara (41) scores a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half at Caesars Superdome. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants’ run defense, in Harbaugh’s words, has been “feast or famine” this season.
