The Giants’ run defense, in Harbaugh’s words, has been “feast or famine” this season. Last week in the tie against Washington, it was clearly the latter, having surrendered a season-high 202 yards on the ground. There are many reasons for the Giants’ struggles in run defense, but one glaring issue has been facing pre-snap motion. Motion changes the look for the defense and has sometimes left players out of position or forced them into bad angles as they try to stop the play from gaining a lot of yards. Under head coach Kellen Moore, the Saints have deployed pre-snap motion on 64% of their offensive snaps this season, the ninth-highest rate in the league, and have a 46% success rate overall when using motion. While they use pre-snap motion more in the passing game, they have used it at a 35% rate in the rushing game. If the Giants, who have allowed opponents 5.2 yards per rush attempt on first down, can’t tighten that up, the Saints will have options on subsequent downs, giving New Orleans an advantage. The other thing that could spoil the Giants’ quest to win their fourth straight game at home is their own aggressiveness on defense. If the Giants, who over the last two weeks have blitzed on 57.8% of opposing quarterbacks’ drop backs, come at the Saints with a similar rate of pressure, they’d better hope that Saints signal-caller Tyler Shough, who per PFF data, has a 102.7 passer rating when throwing the ball in 2.5 seconds or less, doesn’t connect with receivers Chris Olave and Rashid Shaheed for the big pass plays downfield. If I live to be 100 (fingers crossed), I will never understand how the oddsmakers come up with their weekly point spreads. What I do understand is that Harbaugh has this team dialed in, and this matchup against the Saints is overall favorable for the Giants if they play a relatively clean game and keep the ball-security issues out of the mix. The Giants have a lot more going for them at this point in the season than the Saints, including far too many advantages that, if they hit on all cylinders, will get the job done. Following a frustrating 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the Saints (1-4) have dropped three consecutive games, raising questions about the team's direction under second-year head coach Kellen Moore. The struggles have even drawn the attention of team owner Gayle Benson , who recently expressed frustration with the organization's performance and made it clear that continued losing would not be tolerated without consequences. With expectations rising and patience wearing thin, New Orleans faces another difficult challenge against a surprising Giants team that has emerged as an early contender in the NFC East. Here are our predictions for Sunday's game. Grant Chachere, Staff Writer: L 24-17 This is the Saints' first road game since Week 2, and it’s a strategic one at that, as the Saints will immediately fly out of New York for their game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris next week. However, this is a critical game for coach Kellen Moore , and maybe even longtime general manager Mickey Loomis . I don’t think Tyler Shough will have many games like he did last week in the loss to the Vikings, but he will have another matchup against a top-10 defense as the Giants are ninth in total defense. The strength of the defense is its ability to defend the pass, allowing only 199.7 yards per contest, which is good for seventh in the NFL, and have forced six interceptions, which is good for fourth. While I think Shough will do much better, the Giants have the players needed to at least limit Shough, and New Orleans’ rushing attack is one of the NFL’s worst and will be ineffective. While the Giants have struggled to stop the run, they will have no trouble stopping the Saints. At the half, join us for Halftime Studs & Duds . Then, a fter the game, join us for our Biggest Winners & Biggest Losers , our View of the Game , and the Most Important Quotes from Kellen Moore & Players . Defensively, I think the Saints will do enough to keep the game close but not enough to win. The Giants aren’t the greatest offense in the world, but Cam Skattebo is a decent running back, while the receiving threats of Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are going to give the Saints’ defense a heap of trouble. I predict a one-score game in the Meadowlands with the Giants pulling it out. Prediction: Giants 24, Saints 17 Doug Joubert, Publisher: W 21-17 Which Saints club will show in the Meadowlands today? Will it be the one from the first three weeks of the season, or the one from the last three? We know this: those leading this organization have been put on notice by the woman that holds the checkbook. For the first time as owner of the Saints, Gayle Benson is faced with a situation that will require resolve and a possible move that will force her to make decisions that will be uncomfortable. She has put her trust and belief in those in charge. After seeing where her club has gone in the last few weeks, and the fan reaction to that direction, Mrs. Benson is having to rethink that trust. Meanwhile, a two-week road trip followed by the Saints open/bye week may be just what the doctor ordered for Moore and his troops: a chance to regroup and rethink where things are. Being a "glass-half-full" kinda guy, I'm getting this feeling this may be the first step to Moore, his coaches, and his players turning things around. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Saints are 1.5-point favorites over the Giants on the spread, with the over/under set at 45.5 total points. New Orleans is a -115 moneyline favorite to win outright, while New York is listed as a -105 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Saints vs Giants predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, October 18. Saints vs Giants pick: Saints -1.5 (+100) My Giants vs. Saints best bet is New Orleans to cover the spread (-1.5), with the best price currently available at FanDuel . Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Download the Action Network app now for more NFL picks and analysis! Saints vs Giants Odds for NFL Week 6 Saints vs Giants spread: Saints -1.5, Giants +1.5 Saints vs Giants total: over/under 45.5 Saints vs Giants moneyline: Saints -115, Giants -105 New Orleans Saints vs New York Giants Preview The Saints originally opened as underdogs for this game, but almost immediately swung to 1.5-point road favorites — and I think they are sitting at the absolute bottom of their market value. Am I thrilled to back New Orleans on the road here? Not exactly. But I am itching to fade the Giants . Sure, the Saints' run defense is abysmal, but they are facing a Giants team entirely incapable of exploiting it. New Orleans has played a grueling schedule the last two weeks, facing the Falcons (who ran wild with Bijan Robinson) and the Vikings (who have one of the best defenses in the NFL). Offensively, Tyler Shough has been very good when kept clean in the pocket. With the Giants missing Brian Burns , Shough should have all day to operate and consistently move the ball through the air in this game. The Giants are a couple games above .500, but they are arguably the most fraudulent team in the NFL. They could easily be 1-4 right now after lucking out with a tie against the Commanders last week. New York's back-to-back home wins came against the Titans and Cardinals — two incompetent teams that turned the ball over at the goal line with a chance to win. Offensively, the Giants have completely stalled since losing Jaxson Dart. They rank 29th in both rush success rate and rush EPA, meaning their ground game has almost totally vanished. Jameis Winston has thrown for 694 yards with a 6:3 TD:INT ratio in the three games he's started. He's done a good job of feeding Malik Nabers as the Giants' WR1 has surpassed 100 receiving yards in each of the last two weeks. Of course, the thing with Winston is that he's prone to making critical mistakes when throwing into zone coverage. Saints vs Giants Pick, Betting Analysis There is a massive strength-of-schedule disparity here, with the Giants feasting on the easiest schedule in the league so far while the Saints have been heavily battle tested against some of the NFL's best. Without Jaxson Dart's mobility, the Giants simply haven't bee able to run the ball with Cam Skattebo, forcing Jameis Winston into high-variance, mistake-prone dropbacks. The Saints should be able to keep the pocket clean for Tyler Shough throughout this game, which will likely allow him to dissect the Giants' defense and lift his team to a road win. We're breaking down the final New Orleans Saints injury report for Week 6's road game against the New York Giants . Who's in, who's out, and who has a chance to play? The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? Starting DT Vernon Broughton (illness) was limited, bringing the number of Saints players still under the weather from the weekend to three. Long snapper Zach Wood (calf) was designated to return to practice. Saints' first injury report of NFL Week 6 includes multiple players dealing with illness from last weekend Skip to content College Football Close Menu All College Football The New Orleans Saints have begun their week of practice leading up to their Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants. They were without a handful of key players due to illness. Saints' Wednesday injury report for NFL Week 6 Giants' Wednesday injury report for NFL Week 6 Starting EDGE Abdul Carter (calf), starting right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), starting cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) starting safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and starting left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) all missed Wednesday's practice. Giants coach John Harbaugh said Carter is “doing very well,” but his status for Sunday now must come into question. Eluemunor, Hood, and Nubin are considered day-to-day. home.headline: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out?
home.blurb: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? We're breaking down the final New Orleans Saints injury report for Week 6's road game against the New York Giants . Who's in, who's out, and who has a chance to play? The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers won ugly against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday and a big story coming out of the game was the return of two veteran stalwarts in the trenches who played very well in their first game back in right tackle Taylor Moton and defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton. Moton’s return couldn’t have come at a better time. While Moton was sidelined, rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling served as the team’s starting right tackle over the first four games. However, Freeling suffered a knee injury in Week 4 and wasn’t able to play on Sunday, opening the door for Moton to step back into his starting spot. Once Freeling is cleared, that’s where the conversation gets interesting. The Panthers would like to continue developing Freeling and have him out on the field. But, Moton isn’t a player you’re taking off the field and left tackle Rasheed Walker is coming off his best game of the season after allowing one pressure on 46 pass-blocking snaps. “There’s a bunch of scenarios we’re still working through,” Canales explained. “T-Mo looked like T-Mo, Rasheed Walker played his best game, we’ll see where Monroe is at physically. And we’ll go from there. This is a first-round pick for us, this is a high value player for us. We’re going to do what’s best for the Panthers and put the best group and healthiest group out there. That’s a good challenge for Monroe to see how he responds to the training, the treatment, and to see if he shows us how ready he is to play and then how do we play him.” Step one is getting Freeling healthy. After that, it does become a difficult decision because Freeling was playing at a high level for a rookie that came into the league with limited experience. This was supposed to be a red-shirt year essentially for Freeling with him getting limited reps as a swing tackle. Plans obviously changed given Moton’s situation earlier in the year and Freeling stepped up in a major way. “That’s something that we are thinking about,” Canales added. “When you have guys playing high quality football, of course Monroe was a part of that group when he was playing at the right tackle. We know we have options. My dad always said ‘A man with options is blessed,’ but again we have to do what’s right for the team. We take this seriously. Monroe wants to be out there. He’s itching and he’s working really hard.” This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. home.blurb: Commanders' Terry McLaurin Suffers Devastating Injury Before Eagles Game Unlock the latest Heavy on Eagles news — direct to your inbox. Updated Oct 20, 2026 at 10:16am The Philadelphia Eagles aren't the only NFC East team to deal with major injuries this season. Across the division, the Washington Commanders have been in a similar boat. The star quarterback, Jayden Daniels, missed time with a notable setback. Although he's back, the team has now lost its star wide receiver, Terry McLaurin, to a knee injury. According to reports, Terry McLaurin's season is coming to an early end. “Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that the team feared a “significant” injury after the game and that McLaurin would go for tests on Tuesday to determine just how significant it is. Those tests are pending, but Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that the team is bracing to learn that McLaurin will miss the rest of the season,” Pro Football Talk reported on Tuesday, October 20 . The 31-year-old speedy wideout has been one of the most consistent receivers in the NFL during his tenure in Washington. The former Ohio State standout has given the Eagles' secondary trouble in the past. However, Philly won't face McLaurin the next time around. Before going down with his injury, McLaurin appeared in five games. Over that stretch, he was targeted 27 times, catching 15 passes for 230 yards and one score. Before going down against the San Francisco 49ers, McLaurin caught one pass for 27 yards. Last season, McLaurin played in just 10 games for the Commanders. He caught 38 passes for 582 yards and three touchdowns. The Eagles and the Commanders are set to face each other for the second and final time this season on Sunday, November 1. When the two teams met in Week 1, the Eagles defeated the Commanders 24-22. At the time, the Eagles were fully healthy. This time around, they are guaranteed to be without Jalen Hurts–and could potentially miss others. home.headline: NFL fans react to Michael Robinson’s apology to Eagles’ Jalen Hurts
home.blurb: Recall that Robinson had a horrible take on Hurts' injury situation last week, before all the details came to light. He insinuated that Hurts was merely opting out of playing because his team was struggling. NFL fans react to Michael Robinson apology to Eagles' Jalen Hurts CBB Twitter Instagram Youtube Linkedin NFL fans react to Michael Robinson's apology to Eagles' Jalen Hurts Was it enough to mitigate Michael Robinson's horrific and highly inappropriate take on the Jalen Hurts situation? By Wendi Oliveros NFL Network's Michael Robinson issued an apology via social media to Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts on Monday, Oct. 19. The blowback from his comment was fast and furious. Robinson's rant aged horribly as the scary details of Hurts' blood clots came to light on Monday. MORE: Former Eagles receiver sends prayers to Jalen Hurts after health scare NFL Network’s Michael Robinson accused Jalen Hurts of FAKING injuries so he doesn’t get blamed for his team’s struggles 😬 Doctors found multiple blood clots in Jalen Hurts’ lungs. pic.twitter.com/EeKDqaq381 At 8:33 p.m. ET, Robinson posted his apology on X: “I want to sincerely apologize to Jalen Hurts, his family, the Philadelphia Eagles organization and fan base for my comments last Thursday. They were unfounded and I never should have speculated on a health issue of a player or his commitment to his team.” My official apology to @JalenHurts @Eagles and the entire fanbase. My comments were wrong. No excuse. https://t.co/fhHW2VFT39 The timing of the post is intriguing as football fans were likely watching the Monday Night Football game between the Washington Commanders and San Francisco 49ers. Those not watching the game were likely watching the Tampa Bay Rays win Game 6 of the ALCS and punch their ticket to the World Series. MORE: Michael Robinson’s absurd take on Jalen Hurts’ injury looks even more ridiculous now One fan told Robinson he made his comments on TV so his apology should also be on TV. Another fan wrote the apology was not enough. “I rarely speak this strongly, but you should be off the air at least for some time. There need to be consequences for these types of terrible comments, assumptions and insinuations, especially given your platform. What an attack on someone’s character and completely unfounded.” Someone noted that Robinson did a “lotta yapping on a network show about Jalen Hurts bailing on his team by using a fake/overblown injury, but a short little bulls–t text post apology on social huh?” A person who isn't an Eagles fan wrote : “This is the weakest/ laziest apology I’ve ever seen.” After his bombastic behavior and inflammatory comments, no apology would probably be good enough, but the consensus is that this one falls short of showing true remorse for what Robinson said. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories on The Big Lead — Freak injury at Panthers practice will cost Jacob Markstrom

home.blurb: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will not play in Week 6 against the Carolina Panthers and he's been ruled out indefinitely due to a blood clot in his calf. Hurts had the injury ahead of Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars and played, but the clot moved this week, leading to the team ruling him out on Thursday. He's since been placed on injured reserve after consultatin with several doctors and experts. Is Jalen Hurts Playing Today? The Eagles opened as 1.5-point favorites at home in this game even though they've been banged up across the board on offense this season. However, Hurts' absence caused this line to flip completely, as the Panthers moved to 3.5-point favorites are now 3-point favorites on the road in the odds at DraftKings . This season, Hurts has completed 57.8 percent of his passes for 933 yards, eight scores and three picks. He's also added 107 rushing yards and a score on the ground. Now that he's on injured reserve, Hurts has to miss at least four games, and it's possible he'll miss more time beyond that. At 2-3, the Eagles' playoff hopes are hanging in the balance, as they're now +385 to win the NFC East (third in the odds) and +320 to make the playoffs. Both of those numbers have fallen considerably with Hurts on injured reserve. Even though Carolina is favored in this Week 6 matchup, one of SI Betting's editors is high on McKee as the Eagles' backup. Here's a look at our favorite prop bet for this NFC battle on Sunday. Hurts' play has been one of the downfalls of the Eagles' offense, so someone new under center may lead to good things, especially considering how well backup quarterbacks have played in their first starts across the league so far this season. It's also worth noting that the Panthers haven't exactly been an elite defense so far this season. They rank 20th in opponent dropback EPA and 21st in opponent dropback success rate. The Bucs beat the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last week, but now, they'll face a tougher defense and a legendary quarterback in Aaron Rodgers. As always, our staff has made its picks for Sunday's big cross-conference matchup in Tampa Bay. Here's how we see the Bucs' game against the Steelers shaping out: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Steelers 24, Bucs 20 The Bucs are coming off their first win of the season, and they have an excellent chance to continue that momentum against the Steelers. I expect the Bucs to continue being efficient on offense, so it will be up to the defense to stop Warren and not allow the playmakers for the Steelers to make big plays. I think the Bucs do, but aren’t able to come away with a clutch play that would give them the win. Overall Record: 3-2 James Hill, Writer: Steelers 21, Bucs 17 I believe this will be a low-scoring affair, as both defenses have the chance to be good. However, I give the nod to Aaron Rodgers over Jalon Daniels, who will get a start once more with Mayfield on the mend. Overall record: 2-3 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 21, Steelers 14 So far, the 2026 NFL season has been very deflating for a Buccaneers team that had plenty of optimism heading into it. But because they play in the NFC South, the Buccaneers aren’t dead yet. However, if they have any hope of turning their season around and eventually making a push for the playoffs, they need to build some momentum off their first victory of the year in Dallas last week. Defensively, the Bucs match up pretty well with the Steelers. Tampa Bay's corners have played out of their minds this season, and this will be their easiest matchup yet. That should allow Bowles to really sell out to stop the run led by Jaylen Warren, who has developed into the Steelers’ most dynamic offensive weapon. Jalon Daniels and Zac Robinson need to take care of the football and control the clock like they did against Dallas. If they can, the Bucs will win. Logan Robinson, Founder: Steelers 31, Bucs 24 This front seven for the Steelers is going to be a lot different than what Jalon Daniels has faced this season. Zac Robinson will want to get the run game going again with Bucky Irving, but it won’t be easy with Cam Heyward and others in the middle for Pittsburgh. I think this is a great game to take advantage of an immobile Aaron Rodgers and find multiple sacks throughout. If you can’t find sacks in this game, you’ve got issues going into the rest of the season. I think the Bucs keep this one close against a dinged-up Steelers team but don’t pull it off in the fourth quarter. River Wells, Editor: Steelers 24, Bucs 17 The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got a huge win against the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last Thursday, and now, they'll try to pick up another with quarterback Jalon Daniels under center. The good news? This offense isn't nearly as good as Dallas' offense. The bad news? The defense is much better. The Bucs put up 24 against a paltry Dallas defense, so they should put up less against a more competent unit. T.J. Watt, with 4.5 sacks in five games, will be the best edge rusher the Bucs have faced so far this year, and he'll probably make Daniels' life hell for four quarters. On the offensive side for the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers' quick-fire short game matches up perfectly against Bowles' defense. Jaylen Warren is arguably the most dynamic player the Bucs have faced this year since Ja'Marr Chase, and he'll give Tampa Bay's defense fits, too. The Bucs could keep this close, but I think Pittsburgh takes it. Consensus: Steelers 4, Bucs 1 The Bucs got it done against Dallas, but most of our panel doesn't think they can get it done against the Steelers back at home. Will Daniels and the Bucs make it two in a row for the first time since the beginning of the 2025 season? Or will the Steelers knock the Bucs down to 1-5 on the year? picks.blurb: Prediction For Buccaneers' Week 6 Clash Against the Pittsburgh Steelers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NBA Predictions World Series schedule Week 7 Waiver Wire 49ers are 6-0 Reese, Dream get even Prediction For Buccaneers' Week 6 Clash Against the Pittsburgh Steelers (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Jason Klingensmith Sun, October 18, 2026 at 6:13 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally got their first victory of the season last week, but must go on a winning streak in order to make it meaningful. At 1-4, the Bucs are only 1.5 games behind the Carolina Panthers in the weak NFC South division. However, Tampa must win a few more games before it can even start thinking about making the playoffs. Luckily, the Bucs have winnable games on the schedule over the next few weeks, including a pair against division rivals. However, Tampa has the Pittsburgh Steelers on the docket next, already the Bucs' third game against an AFC North foe. The Steelers are 3-2 and have been inconsistent this season, although their offense has turned a corner after a very slow start. The Bucs are 2.5-point underdogs at home, but managed to pull off the upset against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5 as 9.5-point underdogs. Beating the Steelers will qualify as an upset, but it is a very winnable game for the Bucs. Aside from a non-existent pass rush, the Bucs' defense has been very good this season. Now it must contend with a red-hot Aaron Rodgers, who has thrown for three TDs in each of Pittsburgh's last three games. Steelers' RB Jaylen Warren has also been outstanding in the last three games, rushing for 127, 93, and 101 yards. He also caught an 80-yard TD last week, and his 230 receiving yards lead the team. Tampa's run defense is second in the NFL so far, and stopping Warren is one of my five keys to a Bucs' victory , as is finally getting the pass rush to show a pulse. On offense, the Bucs have a budding star in RB Bucky Irving, who is coming off a career-best 165 rushing yards and had both a rushing and a receiving TD against Dallas. For Tampa to win, Irving must continue to be the centerpiece of the offense. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will be making his third straight start while starting QB Baker Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb. Daniels has played with the poise of a seasoned veteran and earned the first victory of his career against the Cowboys. For Tampa to win, Daniels must once again play a clean, turnover-free game. The offensive line must keep Pittsburgh's pass rush, especially T.J. Watt, away from Daniels. This game is set to be a matchup of strengths against strengths. Warren is sixth in the NFL in rushing yards and will be going up against Tampa's strong run defense. Rodgers has been great over the last three weeks, but will have to make plays against a secondary that has shut down the star WR duos of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The Steelers will be without WRs Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson in this game. If Irving can get going early, it will make life much easier for Daniels, whose ability to also make plays with his legs can be a huge factor, especially on third down. This game seems like it could go either way, with a turnover or missed kick looming large at game's end. I don't think it will be Chase McLaughlin who misses the kick, as he has been perfect this season for the Bucs. Prediction: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 22

away.blurb: Three Pittsburgh Steelers have been ruled out for the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, and five more are questionable to suit up, according to the team's Friday injury report. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back this week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Wilson had a large wrap on his left hand after the game. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Fellow wide receiver DK Metcalf was initially listed as questionable to play after missing practice on Friday with an illness, but he has now been cleared to play. Tight end Pat Freiermuth is also questionable to play after suffering a calf injury in practice on Saturday. Strong safety DeShon Elliott remains limited in practice and will not return this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. He is listed as questionable. away.headline: Buccaneers vs. Steelers: Final injury report for Week 6
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. home.headline: Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield may try to return from injury for Panthers game
home.blurb: It sounds like Mayfield could attempt to return to the lineup when the Buccaneers play at the 3-2 Carolina Panthers on Oct. 25. Bowles previously said that Mayfield would likely be sidelined for "a minimum of three weeks" due to his setback, but a subsequent report noted that the signal-caller wanted to return after just two missed games. Such a scenario didn't play out, but Ira Kaufman of the JoeBucsFan website noted on Monday that "even Baker Mayfield detractors can’t muster a sensible argument to keep him sidelined once he is healed from a dislocated right thumb" following what happened at Tampa Bay's Raymond James Stadium on Sunday afternoon. A Tampa Bay Buccaneers side that has been without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield since he went down with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand in Week 3 fell to 1-5 on the season when it squandered a 16-3 lead en route to suffering a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Buccaneers will evaluate Baker Mayfield "during the week" ahead of Panthers game Per Josh Alper of Pro Football Talk, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles confirmed on Monday that Mayfield is on track to practice this coming Wednesday. "He’s supposed to practice Wednesday," Bowles said about Mayfield. "We’re gonna take a good look at him there, and we’ll kind of evaluate him during the week and see how he does." U ndrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has served as Tampa Bay's temporary QB1 since the club's Week 4 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Oct. 4. While Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown to help Tampa Bay earn a stunning 24-16 victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Oct. 8, he came back down to earth when he tossed a pair of interceptions and took five sacks in the Buccaneers' loss to the Steelers. Buccaneers will try to get Baker Mayfield, Jalon Daniels ready for Panthers game "Both will be in the meetings, obviously," Bowles added about Mayfield and Daniels. "Both will be in the meetings, and we’ll see how the week goes before we decide who it is." After Bowles offered his Mayfield update, DraftKings Sportsbook had the Buccaneers on Monday as three-point underdogs against the Panthers. Want more articles like this? away.headline: Rams Make Decision on Blake Grupe Following Injury vs Cardinals
away.blurb: Grupe had one field goal opportunity against the Arizona Cardinals in Sunday's loss, converting from 44 yards in the first quarter. On the ensuing kickoff, he pushed returner Devin Duvernay out of bounds, suffering a knee injury in the process . He immediately came out of the game, doubtful to return, and left the stadium in a leg brace. ESPN's Adam Schefter reports Grupe tore his ACL. Reporting from Los Angeles Tuesday, October 20 LA Sports Report Daily inbox intelligence from LA Sports Report Dodgers More teams ▾ Angels Galaxy LAFC Angel City The Los Angeles Rams placed kicker Blake Grupe, who signed with the team Tuesday, on injured reserve following an injury he sustained Sunday. The Rams are yet to replace him on the roster. What Happened to the Rams' Kicking Unit? Los Angeles felt Grupe's absence in the loss, as they strayed away from kicking for most of the remainder of the game. They opted to go for two following a second-quarter touchdown, failing the attempt, and turned the ball over on downs on the Cardinals' 27-yard line in the third quarter rather than kicking a 44-yard field goal. Punter Ethan Evans hit a PAT to give the Rams a one-point lead with less than a minute left in the fourth quarter, but the Cardinals stormed down the field to hit a field goal and win by a score of 18-16. This incident came less than a week after the Rams waived their previous kicker, Harrison Mevis , due to his inaccuracy in last week's Monday Night Football loss to the Buffalo Bills. Neither of Mevis' two looks last week went through the sticks, one being a game-tying effort in overtime, which the Bills blocked. Without a kicker on their roster, the Rams are sure to make a pickup with Grupe sidelined. The Rams are off to a rough start to the season, as they currently have a 2-4 record through six games and sit last in the NFC West. Despite their sour record, though, the Rams have been among the best offensively and defensively in the NFL. They'll get an opportunity to bounce back from a rough few weeks on Sunday, when they face off against the Las Vegas Raiders, who have lost each of their last three games following a 3-0 start. Kickoff for that game comes at 1:25 p.m. PT. away.headline: Injury Report, Week 6 vs. Cardinals: Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl questionable
away.blurb: Rams Injury Report, Week 6 vs. Cardinals: Cornerback Trent McDuffie and safety Kam Curl questionable Skip to main content Primary nav TEAM WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. – Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cardinals at SoFi Stadium (1:05 p.m. PT, FOX). Head coach Sean McVay said McDuffie's groin injury popped up after he "felt a little something" in his groin at the end of Thursday's practice. McDuffie did not practice Friday in what McVay indicated was a precautionary approach being taken. Safety Kam Curl (ankle) is also listed as questionable for Week 6, but McVay said they "feel good about him." McVay said Curl's ankle injury stemmed from "soreness" from Monday night's game against the Bills. McVay also said tight end Davis Allen (foot), who was limited in Friday's practice, is "trending in the right direction." Allen was later listed without a game status designation on Friday's injury report. For the Cardinals, running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is among three players ruled out, while punter Blake Gillikin (back) is one of four players listed as questionable. *The Rams did not practice on Wednesday; participation that day is an estimation. news Rams Injury Report, Week 5 vs. Bills: Aaron Donald, Colby Parkinson and Jaylen Watson good to go for Monday Night Football; Quentin Lake questionable but 'trending in the right direction' news Injury Report, Week 4 at Eagles: Puka Nacua and Kamren Kinchens good to go; Colby Parkinson questionable; Terrance Ferguson, Jaylen Watson and Aaron Donald ruled out news Rams Injury Report, Week 3 at Broncos: Puka Nacua and Kam Kinchens doubtful for Sunday Night Football news Rams Injury Report, Week 2 vs. Giants: Kam Kinchens ruled out, Jordan Whittington doubtful and Puka Nacua questionable for Monday Night Football vs. Giants news Rams Injury Report, Week 1 vs. 49ers: Aaron Donald only player ruled out among those listed; no designation for Myles Garrett news Injury Report, NFC Championship Game: Rob Havenstein ruled out; Byron Young questionable but expected to play news Injury Report, Wild Card round at Panthers: Kevin Dotson and Jordan Whittington ruled out; Terrance Ferguson and Josh Wallace questionable news Injury Report, Week 18 vs. Cardinals: Josh Wallace, Kevin Dotson and Quentin Lake ruled out; Blake Corum, Davante Adams, Alaric Jackson, Omar Speights, Tyler Higbee and Kyren Williams questionable news Injury Report, Week 17 at Falcons: Kevin Dotson and Josh Wallace ruled out while Davante Adams is doubtful for Monday Night Football; Alaric Jackson and Braden Fiske questionable news Injury Report, Week 16 at Seahawks: Davante Adams doubtful, Braden Fiske questionable for Thursday Night Football Stu Jackson Senior Staff Writer Below are the final injury reports for both teams. away.headline: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed
away.blurb: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB OUT For Week 6 Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Jeremiyah Love has battled an ankle injury throughout the season, and the ailment will keep the running back sidelined for Week 6. The Arizona Cardinals gave him the most guaranteed money of any running back in NFL history when they selected him with the third-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , and it's easy to see why. The Notre Dame product dominated at the collegiate level, routinely flashing his elite athleticism and ability to make plays both as a runner and a returner. In theory, he has the talent to be a true three-down workhorse like Atlanta's Bijan Robinson and Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs . Unfortunately for everyone involved, Jeremiyah Love suffered an ankle injury during his first real taste of NFL action. The running back suffered an ankle injury midway through the contest and missed most of the preseason. While he has played in five games despite the injury, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport revealed the running back will not play in Week 6, as the team is resting him in hopes of ensuring his long-term health. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor While Jeremiyah Love has played in every game this season, he hasn't lived up to his pre-draft hype. So far, the running back has recorded just 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 attempts, good for just 3.7 yards per carry. While the Cardinals passing attack and subpar offensive line certainly haven't done anything to ease the pressure on the rookie, he hasn't looked like his college self either. Hopefully, taking some time to rest will help him recapture his previous form. In his absence, free agent signee Tyler Allgeier will get the start. The former Atlanta Falcon has had similar struggles behind Arizona's offensive line, recording just 119 yards and one touchdown on 35 attempts throughout the young season. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals injury report: Jeremiyah Love sits Wednesday
away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. away.headline: Injury Report: Cardinals Officially Rule 3 Out, 4 Questionable vs Rams
away.blurb: Injury Report: Cardinals Officially Rule 3 Out, 4 Questionable vs Rams Skip to main content SI.COM The Cardinals are officially ruling out Jeremiyah Love (ankle), Wydett Williams (concussion) and Andrew Wingard (knee) ahead of Week 6's battle at SoFi Stadium. Questionable for Arizona is all of Budda Baker (groin), Zaven Collins (hip), Kitan Crawford (ankle) and Blake Gillikin (back). Neither Baker or Collins practiced on Friday while Crawford and Gillikin did in limited fashion. For the Rams, both Kam Curl (ankle) and Trent McDuffie (groin) are questionable entering the weekend. Neither practiced on Friday for Los Angeles. "You got Jimmy Lake as kind of his right hand man in the defensive backfield, so there's definitely technique changes and different coverages and tools that they're using. And then I think just probably building it when when they had Myles [Garrett] too in terms of some of the stuff they were doing. So they throw a lot out at you. I asked him the other day. I said, 'So which one are you going to go with? You go with this, or you going to go with that?' And I just got a little chuckle. So, we'll see, and we'll be ready for it all." ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have a lengthy injury report entering this weekend's clash with the Los Angeles Rams. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur dove deeper into Love's absence, which you can read about here . Off the Cardinals' injury report is all of Carson Beck (back), Devin Duvernay (ribs), Isaac Seumalo (rest) and Josh Sweat (rest). The likes of Davis Allen (foot), Alex Bachman (wrist), Tyler Higbee (rest), Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder), Colby Parkinson (shoulder), Omar Speights (knee), Kegan Trost (hamstring), Josh Wallace (shoulder) and Byron Young (rest) were fully removed from Los Angeles' injury report and are good to go. It's a familiar battle for both sides entering the week, as LaFleur spent the last few seasons under head coach Sean McVay in Los Angeles as the team's offensive coordinator, putting him against Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula. "There's obviously familiarity with just going against him for two of the three years. First year was with Raheem [Morris], but that defense has evolved a lot over the last — since he took over to last year to this year. Obviously, similar foundations and characteristics, but they definitely put their new little twists on it," LaFleur said on facing Shula on Sunday. home.headline: Despite Rams’ awful start, devastating injuries, Super Bowl run still in the cards
home.blurb: Let’s just come right out and ask what everyone is thinking: Is the Rams season already over? Even questionable late-game officiating involving Josh Wallace in two losses cannot excuse everything that happened before those decisive moments. They are 2-4 this year, but with three Wild Card spots available, and the NFC looking mostly like a dumpster fire, just reaching the playoffs is not crazy difficult to attain. There’s an age-old adage in sports: Never let a team beat you twice. Well, the Los Angeles Rams apparently never got the memo because not only did they lose to the Arizona Cardinals on the scoreboard on Sunday afternoon, but also on the injury report that was revealed on Monday. The Cardinals delivered a humiliating 18-16 defeat that dropped the Rams to 2-4 and into last place in the NFC West. Then, less than 24 hours later, they were dealt another brutal blow when head coach Sean McVay revealed an avalanche of injuries that was somehow more devastating than the final score. Newly signed kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL making a touchdown-saving tackle after another special teams coverage breakdown. Star receiver Davante Adams ruptured his semitendinosus near his left knee and faces surgery and a six-to-10-week absence. Nose tackle Poona Ford ruptured his triceps and is finished for the season, while defensive end Kobie Turner suffered a groin strain that will sideline him for several weeks. Add those names to a growing injury list featuring Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson and Trent McDuffie, and the Rams now look more like a MASH unit than a team with Super Bowl aspirations. Let’s face it, if there were ever a time to burn sage inside SoFi Stadium and perform an exorcism, this might be it. Between the Rams’ misfortunes and the Chargers’ 0-6 start, things could not get any worse for NFL teams in Los Angeles. “It’s unfortunate we will miss those guys and what they bring on the field,” tight end Tyler Higbee said. “But injuries are part of the game. At the NFL level, everyone is getting paid to do their job. It has to be a next man up mentality.” At some point, the phrase “next man up” stops sounding inspirational and starts sounding like a desperate plea for healthy bodies. Safety Quentin Lake echoed that sentiment, emphasizing the importance of keeping injured teammates involved while preparing their replacements. “It’s now next man up, guys are going to be able to come in and make an impact,” Lake said. Honestly, there’s a compelling argument that it is. This roster was built to win a Super Bowl , not survive a war of attrition. Its greatest strength was elite talent concentrated at critical positions. Now those stars are disappearing faster than McVay can replace them. Worse, the Rams haven’t simply been unlucky. They’ve been undisciplined, inconsistent and occasionally downright incompetent. home.headline: Rams Make Decision on Blake Grupe Following Injury vs Cardinals
home.blurb: Grupe had one field goal opportunity against the Arizona Cardinals in Sunday's loss, converting from 44 yards in the first quarter. On the ensuing kickoff, he pushed returner Devin Duvernay out of bounds, suffering a knee injury in the process . He immediately came out of the game, doubtful to return, and left the stadium in a leg brace. ESPN's Adam Schefter reports Grupe tore his ACL. Reporting from Los Angeles Tuesday, October 20 LA Sports Report Daily inbox intelligence from LA Sports Report Dodgers More teams ▾ Angels Galaxy LAFC Angel City The Los Angeles Rams placed kicker Blake Grupe, who signed with the team Tuesday, on injured reserve following an injury he sustained Sunday. The Rams are yet to replace him on the roster. What Happened to the Rams' Kicking Unit? Los Angeles felt Grupe's absence in the loss, as they strayed away from kicking for most of the remainder of the game. They opted to go for two following a second-quarter touchdown, failing the attempt, and turned the ball over on downs on the Cardinals' 27-yard line in the third quarter rather than kicking a 44-yard field goal. Punter Ethan Evans hit a PAT to give the Rams a one-point lead with less than a minute left in the fourth quarter, but the Cardinals stormed down the field to hit a field goal and win by a score of 18-16. This incident came less than a week after the Rams waived their previous kicker, Harrison Mevis , due to his inaccuracy in last week's Monday Night Football loss to the Buffalo Bills. Neither of Mevis' two looks last week went through the sticks, one being a game-tying effort in overtime, which the Bills blocked. Without a kicker on their roster, the Rams are sure to make a pickup with Grupe sidelined. The Rams are off to a rough start to the season, as they currently have a 2-4 record through six games and sit last in the NFC West. Despite their sour record, though, the Rams have been among the best offensively and defensively in the NFL. They'll get an opportunity to bounce back from a rough few weeks on Sunday, when they face off against the Las Vegas Raiders, who have lost each of their last three games following a 3-0 start. Kickoff for that game comes at 1:25 p.m. PT. home.headline: 3 takeaways from Rams' rash of major injuries suffered in Week 6
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams suffered a multitude of losses over the weekend , with Davante Adams, Poona Ford, and Kobie Turner suffering injuries that will require stints on injured reserve. Turner is considered a short-term absence , while Adams will be out for most of the season , if not all of it. Ford is out for the rest of the year after rupturing his triceps, as will newly signed kicker Blake Grupe. Grupe tore his ACL in his debut while making a tackle. Puka Nacua will be called upon even more with Adams being out for an estimated 6-10 weeks . In the last year of his deal, Nacua has found his form in recent weeks and is making the ultimate push to become the NFL's highest-paid non-quarterback. If he isn't available, for whatever reason, the team is doomed. Max Klare made a lot of sense to draft, and I'm sure Keagen Trost was viewed as the perfect backup swing tackle. CJ Daniels and Tim Keenan III were late-round gambles. However, Daniels has yet to play and Keenan was cut. Klare and Trost should have easy routes towards the starting lineup, but Keenan is gone, and Daniels has to figure out a way to get snaps over Tutu Atwell, who barely gets any himself. With all their losses, here are three takeaways on what they mean for the Rams. Nacua needs to be at his absolute best Not only will the pressure be on him to rise to the occasion, but he won't have Adams to draw some of the attention away from him. However, this is not the biggest issue for the star receiver. While his 2025 season was a statistical success, his story was focused on his off-field behavior and the news that came from it, including a lawsuit that claims Nacua bit a woman on New Year's Eve. Nacua sought professional help for his issues , something many point to as the reason why he hasn't gotten extended yet, even though contemporary Jaxon Smith-Njigba signed his lucrative deal. This is where the Rams need him most. He is the locomotive to their offense, and if he can't perform, the Rams will be on the verge of disaster. Kyren Williams' usage reverted back to how it was to begin the season, having a more even split of carries with Blake Corum. Against the Cardinals, Williams has his fewest carries (10) this season, while his work in the pass game didn't have the same impact as in the past. The reality that the Rams are struggling to accept, even after three years, is that their offensive success is tied to Williams' usage. His utilization impacts linebackers and safeties, giving Nacua and the tight ends the space to open up the pass game. What is even more concerning is that Williams was coming off four straight stellar performances where his effectiveness and the overall effectiveness of the offense only increased with his usage. The fact remains that until Terrance Ferguson returns, Williams is the team's third-best pass catcher. home.headline: Los Angeles Rams are staring down infamy without change that comes in a hurry
home.blurb: The trouble doesn't stop at the standings, either. The Rams are now teetering on the brink of completely falling apart at the seams. Wide receiver Davante Adams is injured and expected to miss around two months of action. Defensive tackle Poona Ford is out for the year. Fellow defensive tackle Kobie Turner is headed to injured reserve. When it rains, it pours. It's raining buckets on the Rams right now. And the 2026 Rams need a quick fix, or else go down as one of the biggest busts of recent memory. That title, right now, belongs to the 2011 Philadelphia Eagle s. The self-proclaimed ‘Dream Team'. Those Eagles finished the 2011 8-8 after backup quarterback Vince Young dubbed the team a ‘Dream Team' — with Philadelphia boasting +600 odds to win the Super Bowl at one point in the offseason. But even that .500 finish is a little misleading. Philadelphia needed a 4-game winning streak at the end of the year just to climb back to an even record. They also started 2-4…just like the 2026 Rams. Los Angeles Rams are staring down infamy without change that comes in a hurry Skip to content College Football Close Menu All College Football The Los Angeles Rams entered 2026 with Super Bowl expectations. A home loss to Arizona and a mounting injury list have changed that conversation in a hurry. Are the Los Angeles Rams bad right now? Unfortunately, the answer is yes. And that puts the Rams on the clock. Not for the NFL Draft, but for infamy. A home loss to the Arizona Cardinals dropped Los Angeles to 2-4. The Cardinals now have as many wins in SoFi Stadium this season as the Rams have in 2026 period. That's a tough pill to swallow. And the medicine will only taste worse from here unless some major changes happen fast. Because infamy is now calling the 2026 Los Angeles Rams. The Los Angeles Rams could supplant the ‘Dream Team' Eagles without some fast changes Los Angeles checked in this summer with +500 to +550 Super Bowl odds, making them an even heavier favorite than the 2011 Eagles. So the pressure is on. The injury report isn't doing Los Angeles any favors, either. Losing Adams strips away a key piece of the passing game. Losing Ford and Turner in the same stretch takes two important bodies away from the defensive front. That's a lot of talent to replace for a team that can't afford many more losses. The Rams have time to fix this. Six games is not a full season. But they're on the clock. Avoid falling into the same trap the Eagles did 15 years ago, or risk taking their place as the most disappointing team of the millennium. home.headline: Rams engulfed in injury crisis as Super Bowl favorites lose four players including Davante Adams
home.blurb: Adams is now expected to be out for six to ten weeks, meaning he could be back as late as Week 16 of the season. Rams defensive tackle Poona Ford has been ruled out for the season after rupturing his triceps. Additionally, his fellow DT, Kobie Turner, will be out for between four and six weeks with a groin injury. Finally, kicker Blake Grupe, who was brought in this past week after a horrible kicking performance from Harrison Mevis, is now out for the season with a torn ACL. He hurt himself while making a tackle on a kickoff return. The Los Angeles Rams announced four devastating injuries across the span of just seven minutes, which will see key contributors missing significant time. After entering the season as the odds-on favorites to win the Super Bowl , the Rams have sunk to a 2-4 record following a defeat to the struggling Arizona Cardinals on a walk-off field goal. Now, the four injuries announced on Monday afternoon cast serious doubts on the Rams' ability to recover their season. The biggest name joining the injury report is star wide receiver Davante Adams, who tore his hamstring, according to Rams head coach Sean McVay. The wideout hurt himself while running a route before coming up lame without any contact on him at all. With this news, the Rams have now lost their leader in receiving yards (480) and receiving touchdowns (four) for this season. Immediately after announcing the Adams news, McVay revealed three other devastating injuries. Ford and Turner combined for 37 total tackles while Ford also tallied a tackle for a loss this season. At the time of publishing, the Rams officially have eight players on injured reserve, including superstar pass rusher Myles Garrett. Additionally, top cornerback Trent McDuffie missed this past Sunday's game with a groin injury. Jordan Whittington is now projected to replace Adams at the WR2 spot while the pass rush is expected to be operated by Braden Fiske, Ty Hamilton and Aaron Donald. It's unclear what direction will be taken at the kicking position.

picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Chargers: NFL Week 6 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the third time in five games to begin the 2026-27 season, the Kansas City Chiefs will square off against an opponent from their own division. Coming out of the bye, it's the Los Angeles Chargers who stroll into Arrowhead Stadium to face Andy Reid's group. With Kansas City looking to maintain an undefeated record and Los Angeles' season hanging on by the thinnest of threads, many would assume that this has the makings of a blowout. Given how close these rivals usually play each other, though, is there the possibility of a more competitive Sunday showdown? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 6 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Undefeated vs. winless doesn’t really mean all that much to me once game day actually arrives. The Chiefs are coming off a bye, but they're still dealing with an array of impactful injuries . The Chargers are limping toward their week off, but it’s a divisional game. I don't expect the Chargers to magically find offensive success against the Chiefs, yet I could easily see this game being uglier than Chiefs fans would like. Jordan Foote: Kansas City is well rested for Week 6, and Reid's track record after a bye speaks for itself. Not only that, but the Chargers are struggling in two of the game's three phases (offense and special teams) and are extremely banged up to boot. This team is undoubtedly more talented than its record shows , which is why I'm calling for an ugly one-score game, but the hosts should be able to overcome their own injuries and rise to 5-0 on the still-young season. If the Chiefs lose this one, they have only themselves to blame. There's ample room for a hint of a nail-biter, albeit not an embarrassing loss to a floundering foe. Joshua Schulman: An undefeated Chiefs squad taking on a winless Chargers team feels like the biggest trap game of all time, but it’s hard to fathom just how bad Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel's unit has been. While they’ve been trending up in recent weeks, poor late-game execution and costly turnovers have sunk their chances. Coming off a bye, I think the old “rest vs. rust” debate will play out for the Chiefs offense, and Patrick Mahomes may need some time to connect with his new targets now that Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton won’t be suiting up. However, they should come alive in the second half, and the defense will do enough to keep it close the first few quarters. Tyler Brown: Early in the week, this one felt closer than the records suggest. Chiefs-Chargers games have a history of being tight regardless of the circumstances, and that reputation is hard to shake. The longer the week went on, though, the harder it became to make a case for Los Angeles. This Chargers team is much closer to the Miami Dolphins the Chiefs dispatched 24-10 in Week 3 than they are to any legitimate AFC West contender. The injury report alone, with Joe Alt, Rashawn Slater, and Derwin James all out, makes this a mismatch. Add in the 0-5 record and four rookie offensive linemen protecting Herbert, and the case for a competitive game falls apart. The sack drought ends Sunday. Herbert has been sacked 30 times in 11 career games against Kansas City, and he's never faced this Chiefs defensive line with this little protection. Three to four sacks feels conservative, and one or two turnovers wouldn't be surprising. Walker should have another big day on the ground, and tight end Travis Kelce will get going without James lurking in the middle of the field. The young receivers will have a chance to build some chemistry with Mahomes in a low-stakes environment. Justin Herbert and the Chargers have yet to win a game this season, going from a preseason darling to one of the worst teams in the NFL. Not only are the Chargers winless, but they have yet to cover the spread and rank in the bottom half of the league in almost every key metric. So, this isn’t a case of a tough schedule messing up L.A.’s playoff chances. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are undefeated and appear to be back in the mix for the No. 1 seed in the AFC after a six-win 2025 campaign. Kenneth Walker III has totally transformed a Kansas City offense that ranks in the top-10 in the league in EPA/Play, yards per play and success rate in 2026. Oddsmakers have set Mahomes and Co. as massive favorites at home in this AFC West clash, but can they cover? All season long, the SI Betting team is predicting the final score of every NFL game – a fun way to help bettors decide on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, there’s a chance that we’ll hit an exact score in the process! This AFC West matchup has major implications for the Chiefs as they eye the No. 1 seed in the conference, especially since they already had their bye. Chargers vs. Chiefs Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan has taken on the challenge of betting on every NFL game this season in his Road to 272 column . Earlier this week, he explained why he’s taking the OVER in this matchup: Don't look now, but the Patrick Mahomes-led Chiefs once again have one of the best offenses in football. They lead the league in yards per play, averaging 6.5 yards per snap, and they also rank fourth in EPA per play and fifth in offensive success rate. Led by Offensive Player of the Year favorite Kenneth Walker, they're a dangerous offense to face, and any game they're involved in shouldn't have a total in the low 40s. Unfortunately, the Chargers' offense is bad, but I continue to believe that Mike McDaniel's system is going to eventually click, and they're going to have some strong offensive outputs sooner rather than later. Now that they face an average Chiefs defense facing an 0-6 record to start the season, now could be the time that their offense comes out firing. While I don’t mind the OVER play, I think this is going to be a lopsided game, especially since Los Angeles is banged up across the board on offense. Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris have all been hurt in 2026, and the Chargers have tackle Rashawn Slater on injured reserve. That’s led to a terrible offense, as L.A. ranks 32nd in the NFL in EPA/Play and 28th in success rate through five weeks. As MacMillan mentioned, this Chiefs offense has been one of the best in the league, and I expect Patrick Mahomes and Co. to take care of business out of a bye week against a Chargers team that has a very slim chance of turning this season around. away.headline: Chargers get major Ladd McConkey injury update before Chiefs game
away.blurb: Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has no injury designation for Sunday’s game, clearing the way for his expected return after dealing with a lingering foot injury. ESPN’s Adam Schefter confirmed the development Friday, citing the Chargers’ final injury report. The announcement comes after McConkey was limited during practice Wednesday and Thursday while continuing to recover from an injury that has affected his availability in recent weeks. McConkey was listed as questionable ahead of last Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos. Although he was active for the game, the receiver did not play a single offensive snap. McConkey’s return could provide a much-needed boost to quarterback Justin Herbert and a Chargers passing attack that has struggled to establish consistency. While McConkey has been cleared to play, it remains unclear whether he will immediately return to his usual workload after dealing with a lingering foot injury. The Los Angeles Chargers received encouraging news Friday as they prepare for an important AFC West matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Los Angeles ultimately suffered a 23-17 loss, continuing a difficult start to the season. Through four appearances this season, McConkey has recorded 12 receptions for 183 yards and one touchdown. Those numbers represent a disappointing start for a receiver who established himself as one of Herbert’s most reliable targets during his first two NFL seasons. However, injuries have played a significant role in limiting his opportunities. The Chargers have also dealt with health concerns involving several other receivers, including Quentin Johnston, Tre’ Harris and Brenen Thompson. Johnston has been managing a chest injury, while Harris suffered a hamstring injury during the loss to Denver. Those setbacks have created additional challenges for Herbert, who has been forced to navigate an offense dealing with injuries at multiple positions. Now, Los Angeles faces another difficult test against Kansas City. Sunday’s matchup against Kansas City presents another challenge for a Chargers team looking to gain momentum in the AFC West. McConkey’s availability gives Justin Herbert a reliable target in the passing game and could provide a much-needed boost to an offense that has struggled with injuries. The Chargers will have to determine how heavily to involve him after his recent injury struggles. For now, Friday’s announcement represents a positive development as Los Angeles prepares to face one of its biggest division rivals. away.headline: Chargers Injury Report: Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston off report vs. Chiefs
away.blurb: Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston were both completely taken off the injury report and should be ready to roll against the Chiefs. Fellow wideouts KeAndre Lambert-Smith and Brenen Thompson were both listed as questionable but both should also be in line to return to the field, though KLS still needs to be activated officially off of IR before Sunday. The other players listed as questionable are defensive tackle Jamaree Caldwell, edge rusher Bud Dupree, linebacker Daiyan Henley, and defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson. Cornerback Rodney Shelley is the lone player with a doubtful tag. Offensive tackle Joe Alt, guard Kayode Awosika, wide receiver Tre' Harris, cornerback Donte Jackson, and safety Derwin James were all ruled out for Sunday. This will be the third missed game for James and the second missed game for Alt who is still receiving opinions on his neck injury he sustained against the Seahawks. *Note that Bud Dupree is listed as both questionable and out. We'll wait for further clarification before adjusting the report. home.headline: Chargers Injury Report: Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston off report vs. Chiefs
home.blurb: Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston were both completely taken off the injury report and should be ready to roll against the Chiefs. Fellow wideouts KeAndre Lambert-Smith and Brenen Thompson were both listed as questionable but both should also be in line to return to the field, though KLS still needs to be activated officially off of IR before Sunday. The other players listed as questionable are defensive tackle Jamaree Caldwell, edge rusher Bud Dupree, linebacker Daiyan Henley, and defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson. Cornerback Rodney Shelley is the lone player with a doubtful tag. Offensive tackle Joe Alt, guard Kayode Awosika, wide receiver Tre' Harris, cornerback Donte Jackson, and safety Derwin James were all ruled out for Sunday. This will be the third missed game for James and the second missed game for Alt who is still receiving opinions on his neck injury he sustained against the Seahawks. *Note that Bud Dupree is listed as both questionable and out. We'll wait for further clarification before adjusting the report.
