home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs' first injury report for Week 6 tilt vs. Los Angeles Chargers shows a team on the mend after the bye week
home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their first injury report ahead of Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers. After having 10 players on the final injury report ahead of the Week 5 bye, Kansas City's roster appears to be on the mend. Rashee Rice didn't participate in practice on Wednesday, but the team removed 5 players who were hurt just two weeks ago from the injury report. For the first time since mid-August, Chiefs LT Josh Simmons took part in a limited practice session. Here’s a quick breakdown of each team's first Week 6 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. They will release game status designations on Friday, Oct. 16. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related As Coach Reid said, Rice did not participate, and Simmons participated in a limited capacity. Simmons moved gingerly in video taken during the open portion of practice ( see FOX 4's footage here ). The Kansas City Chiefs return from their earliest bye of the Patrick Mahomes era facing a 13-week stretch run. A thin wide receiver room and a few rising young players will change the rotation. Buffalo Bills safety CJ Gardner-Johnson has been suspended one game without pay by the NFL over his shameful spitting incident against the Las Vegas Raiders. Gardner-Johnson has since offered a groveling apology for the disgusting moment, in which cameras caught him approaching Raiders tight end Brock Bowers for a heated exchange of words – before spitting in his rival's direction. away.headline: NFL suspends Bills safety Gardner-Johnson for 1 game for spitting at Raiders
away.blurb: After splitting the 2024 season between the Rams and Baltimore, he re-signed with the Bills and had 16 starts last season. He didn't rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. The Bills reached out to White a few weeks ago and targeted the bye week for his return. Buffalo opened up a practice squad spot by releasing cornerback A.J. Woods. ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. (AP) — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardiner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardiner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardiner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons, and signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson's spitting act as being “inexcusable," and said he's discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can't happen. That's not what we're about. That's not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don't need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can't happen. It won't happen again. Personality-wise, I'm not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills announced they're bringing back a familiar face by signing cornerback Tre'Davious White to their practice squad. The 31-year-old White returns for what would be a third stint in Buffalo, and provide the Bills secondary with some much-needed experience. White was selected by Buffalo in the first round of the 2017 draft, and spent his first seven seasons with the Bills before his career was derailed by injuries. See AP’s full NFL coverage here

He didn't rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. The Bills reached out to White a few weeks ago and targeted the bye week for his return. Buffalo opened up a practice squad spot by releasing cornerback A.J. Woods. ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. (AP) — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardiner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardiner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardiner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons, and signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson's spitting act as being “inexcusable," and said he's discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can't happen. That's not what we're about. That's not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don't need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can't happen. It won't happen again. Personality-wise, I'm not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills announced they're bringing back a familiar face by signing cornerback Tre'Davious White to their practice squad. The 31-year-old White returns for what would be a third stint in Buffalo, and provide the Bills secondary with some much-needed experience. White was selected by Buffalo in the first round of the 2017 draft, and spent his first seven seasons with the Bills before his career was derailed by injuries. See AP’s full NFL coverage here

home.blurb: Bills' Final Week 6 Injury Report: DJ Moore, Four Others Questionable to Face Raiders Skip to main content SI.COM The Buffalo Bills have ruled five players as questionable to face the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. One of the 10 without a game designation is starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who left the Week 5 win , and did not return, after 16 snaps due to a back flare-up. Brown practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday before improving to full participation on Thursday and Friday. With a minor "muscle freak out" now in the rearview, the starting right tackle is ready for his 79th regular season appearance in a Bills' uniform. In another positive development, running back Ty Johnson, who was limited by a hamstring at the first two practices, participated in full on Friday, and he's been cleared for the Sunday game. DJ Moore, Ed Oliver return to practice Moore and Oliver both sat out the October 12 win over the Los Angeles Rams after injury incidents knocked them out of the October 4 loss to the New England Patriots. Neither player participated at practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but both returned to the field in a limited capacity on Friday, providing a glimmer of hope that they'll be available for kickoff. "They've been doing a lot on the side. They've been doing all the walkthroughs and everything. It was good to get them out here today, and just being able to move around," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady . "We'll see how they field coming off the field. Look at it on tape. See what it looked like and have discussions. I say it every week, if they're ready to go, they're gonna play." After being scratched in Week 5, Alford and Palmer logged limited participation all three days this week. The former is nursing a minor ankle issue that emerged against the Patriots. The latter is fighting through a shoulder injury from an October 9 practice. Both Alford and Palmer showed positive signs throughout the week, looking ready to return to game action, by multiple accounts, during media-viewing portions of practice. Sanders, who has already dealt with a knee issue and a subsequent bout with appendicitis, made his season debut on October 12. He performed well over 51 defensive snaps, but apparently came out of the overtime win bothered by a shoulder. He progressed to full participation at Friday's practice, but remains questionable to play. Buffalo listed five players as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders , but every player on the active roster still has a chance to play. Four of those questionable players - wide receiver D.J. He does not carry a game designation against Las Vegas. D.J. Moore is questionable after returning to practice Friday. Moore did not practice Wednesday or Thursday before being limited Friday. Ed Oliver is also questionable after returning to practice Friday. Oliver missed practice Wednesday and Thursday before being limited Friday. Joshua Palmer is questionable after being limited all three days this week. Dee Alford is questionable after being limited Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. T.J. Linebacker Terrel Bernard was a full participant Wednesday and Thursday before being limited Friday because of a knee injury, but he is not listed as questionable. Tight end Brock Bowers was limited Wednesday because of a knee injury before practicing fully Thursday and Friday. He is also cleared to play. Hemingway did not practice all week. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The last time these two teams met in Week 4 of the 2025 season, they combined for the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era Getty Images One of the NFL's highest-scoring rivalries will be renewed on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6 when the Green Bay Packers (3-2) host the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) at Lambeau Field on Sunday night. Last season, the Packers traveled down to Texas to face the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, and the two teams tied at 40-40, the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era, since 1996, per CBS Sports Research. The game featured seven lead changes, including six consecutive touchdown drives with a lead change in the second half. However, this rivalry hasn't exactly been very competitive in terms of the games' final outcomes, with the Cowboys seeking their first win against the Packers since the 2016 regular season, quarterback Dak Prescott's rookie year. Since that game, Dallas is 0-5-1 in the last six games against Green Bay despite scoring 31 points per game in that stretch. The problem is their defense has allowed a combined 37 points per game during the six-game winless streak against the Packers. That's the most points per game scored by a team's offense during a six-game winless span against an opponent in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. Sunday will mark Packers quarterback Jordan Love's first home start against the Cowboys, with both of his games against Dallas coming on the road -- a 48-32 wild card round win in the 2023 season and the 40-40 tie last year. It will also mark a homecoming for two former Packers who are now Cowboys: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark and Pro Bowl edge rusher Rashan Gary . Let's dig into this primetime fight against two of the NFL's most historic franchises, but first, here's how you can watch: Where to watch Cowboys vs. Packers Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay, Wisconsin) TV: NBC | Stream: Fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -1.5, O/U 53.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Cowboys vs. Packers need to know Cowboys looking to fix bad vibes on defense: In Week 5, Dallas lost a home game 24-16 on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a team it was favored by 9.5 points. Tampa Bay was starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels , making his second career start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield , and Dallas allowed the Buccaneers to control the game with 241 rushing yards. That was the most for the Buccaneers in a game since the 2024 season. This week, there has been speculation from owner and general manager Jerry Jones about first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker moving upstairs to the booth, but Parker and head coach Brian Schottenheimer maintained he will remain on the sideline. Dallas' performance improvement plan has begun with the hiring of former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant . Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019. Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked defense (395.4 total yards allowed per game), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it. How fixable are the issues? "Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable." Cowboys All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams agrees. "Just from the aspect of the things that we can control are the things that we're messing up on. Effort. Playing with our technique. Playing better, things like that. Those are things we can control as a unit, we can control as a unit. It's fixable. We just have to make our best effort to fix those things. Packers' Jordan Love aims to maintain an explosive passing game to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden : Packers quarterback Jordan Love is fresh off his best game of 2026 in Week 5, a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs. "We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX . "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this." Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards. In total, Love connected on six of eight of his eight throws of 20-plus air yards for a career-high 258 yards and 2 touchdowns on his passes of 20-plus air yards. Per the league's Next Gen stats , only Russell Wilson (264 with the New York Giants in Week 2 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys ) had more in the NGS era (since 2016). According to ESPN Insights , Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006. Slowing this high-flying passing attack down will be a tall task for a struggling Cowboys defense. A stoppable force vs. a movable object: The Packers rank dead last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (60.4) and third-down offense (27.6% conversion rate) thanks to missing running back Josh Jacobs while he was on the commissioner's exempt list and dealing with some offensive line injuries. Across from them on the line of scrimmage at Lambeau Field on Sunday will be the Cowboys' last-ranked run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and last-ranked third-down defense (52.6% conversion rate allowed). Whichever team can find an edge here will likely emerge victorious. New Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr . primed to return in primetime: New Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was set to play his first full game as a Cowboy in Week 5 before a stomach bug made him a late scratch hours before kickoff. However, Porter Jr. is now recovered from his illness and aims to play a full starter's load of snaps. He played on 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans in Week 4 just days after being acquired in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier that week. He is officially listed as questionable to play on Sunday with an ankle injury, but on Wednesday he said he is "definitely" ready to be a full-time starter for Dallas. Parker agreed, saying the team is ready for him to have a "heavily increased" workload against the Packers. Cowboys vs. Packers prediction Despite Porter Jr. likely returning to action for Dallas in Week 6, their defense won't be able to stifle Love, Watson and Golden through the air. Whichever receiver between Watson and Golden that cornerback DaRon Bland , who has struggled with his footing on the field of late, will break free for big gains on a consistent basis. Yes, the Cowboys do have the NFL's No. 7 scoring offense (27.6 points per game) powered by Prescott, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb , wide receiver George Pickens and running back Javonte Williams . However, Dallas' defense struggles will limit their offense's ability to find a rhythm. The Cowboys are averaging 3.07 points per drive, the second-highest by a team under .500 through five games this century per CBS Sports Research, but their 45 drives this season are the second fewest in the league this season. Among the NFL teams that have played in all five weeks of the 2026 season, Dallas' 45 drives stand as the fewest. That's what happens when you have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed). LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. picks.blurb: Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Cowboys vs. Packers on Sunday Night Football in Week 6 Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Sunday’s action in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season closes out with an exciting rivalry matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers, two teams fighting to get into the playoff picture in the NFC. Green Bay is coming off a huge win over the Chicago Bears in Week 5, riding 367 passing yards and two scores from Jordan Love to a second straight victory. The Pack are now 3-2 this season, but they haven’t been impressive on offense for most of the year. Meanwhile, Dallas was shockingly upset in Week 5, losing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and backup quarterback Jalon Daniels on Thursday Night Football. Dallas has the No. 32 defense in the league in EPA/Play, success rate and yards per play allowed, putting a ton of pressure on Dak Prescott and Co. to score on just about every possession. The result for Sunday’s game? A total in the 50s and a very close spread between two teams that have some work to do if they want to make the postseason in the NFC. So, how should we bet on it? All week long, the SI Betting team has made picks for this game, including several player prop selections and anytime touchdown scorer props. To give our readers a quick primer for this game, I’ve compiled all of our top picks into one story ahead of Sunday night’s Cowboys vs. Packers showdown. Let’s dive in! Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Cowboys vs. Packers Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers OVER 52.5 (-105) – Iain MacMillan George Pickens Anytime TD (+150) – Peter Dewey Christian Watson OVER 71.5 Receiving Yards (-115) – Iain MacMillan Jordan Love OVER 271.5 Passing Yards (-113) – Peter Dewey Earlier this week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for this game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s taking the OVER on Sunday night: My strategy for the Cowboys this season is fairly straightforward. If they're favored, bet against them; if they're getting points, take them, if it's close to a pick'em bet the OVER. Their defense is too bad to lay points on them, but their offense is too good to ever underestimate them. That's why, in this week's coin-flip game against the Packers, I'm going to bet the OVER, especially considering the Packers have a similar issue. The two defenses in this game rank 24th and 32nd in opponent success rate, with the Cowboys also ranking 32nd in opponent EPA per play. Let's sit back and root for points on Sunday Night Football. George Pickens had by far his best game of the 2026 season in Week 5, catching nine of his 13 targets for 130 yards and a score. It was the first time in 2026 that Pickens found the end zone, but I think he’s a little undervalued at this price in a potential shootout in Week 6. CeeDee Lamb was banged up at the end of Dallas’ Week 5 loss, and Pickens could take on a lead role for a Cowboys offense that is No. 5 in EPA/Play and No. 4 in total passing yards. Last season, Pickens found the end zone nine times, and he could be due for some positive regression in Week 6 and beyond. MacMillan shares his favorite prop bets of the week in his Player Prop Countdown , and Watson is the No. 4 player in Week 6: Christian Watson has had a breakout season so far in 2026. He enters Week 6 ranking fifth in the NFL in receiving yards, racking up 474 yards for 94.8 per game. Now, he and the Packers get to face arguably the worst defense in the entire league. The Cowboys have given up 8.1 yards per pass attempt, and they also rank last in both opponent dropback EPA and opponent dropback success rate. There couldn't be a better matchup for Jordan Love in Week 6. The Packers quarterback has led the team to the third-most passing yards in the NFL this season, and now he’s taking on Green Bay defense that is last in the NFL in EPA/Play, success rate, EPA/Pass and yards per play allowed. Love has over 271.5 passing yards in three games this season (all over 300 yards), and he already has multiple games with over 40 pass attempts. Getty Dave Holcomb Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:07 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Former Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling has found a new home — again. On Monday, he landed in one of his former homes with a very familiar quarterback. The Athletic's Mike DeFabo reported Monday night the Pittsburgh Steelers plan to sign Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad. The deal will reunite the veteran wideout with quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who he has previously played with in five other seasons. Last year, Valdes-Scantling also joined the Steelers near the midseason point. He caught 10 passes for 80 yards and a touchdown from Rodgers. From 2018-21, he played with the future Hall of Fame quarterback with the Green Bay Packers. This offseason, Valdes-Scantling signed a 1-year, $1.49 million contract with the Cowboys. But Dallas released the veteran at the NFL roster deadline at the end of August. In mid-season, Valdes-Scantling joined the Los Angeles Chargers . The Chargers released the receiver over the weekend. away.headline: Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender
away.blurb: Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. It figures that Winters would get hurt during a game in which he made an impact play with an interception he nearly returned for a touchdown. Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either. The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts. Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning. That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week. Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender Skip to main content SI.COM As if everything else that has gone wrong for the Dallas Cowboys' defense hasn't been enough, the unit has also been ravaged by injuries to make matters worse. The Cowboys are missing starters at cornerback, safety and linebacker, and now they are in danger of losing yet another linebacker from the starting lineup. Last Thursday did not go as planned for Dallas, as the team suffered an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home, but the team gets an opportunity to bounce back in Week 6 with another primetime showdown. This weekend, Dallas will make the trip to Lambeau Field for a Sunday night showdown with the Green Bay Packers . On Thursday afternoon, the Cowboys returned to the practice field and dropped their latest injury report . On Wednesday, five players did not participate in practice, but on Thursday, that number was down to two. home.headline: Green Bay Packers: NFL insider reveals the new Micah Parsons return target
home.blurb: Hopefully, Green Bay can avoid any more serious injuries. On the positive side, they are expecting to get two key contributors back very soon. It has recently been reported that Pro Bowl running back Josh Jacobs will return as the starting running back in Week Seven. Additionally, All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons is getting closer and closer to his own return. NFL insider expects Micah Parsons to return in Week 9 for the Green Bay Packers Initially, many hoped that the All-Pro pass rusher would be able to return for Green Bay’s Week Six matchup against his former team. However, the Packers have not opened up his practice window as they want to ensure that he is 100% healthy and not at risk for any soft tissue injuries because of rushing a return to the field. “A league source tells me Parsons might not return until Week 9, against the Patriots on Nov. 8. The Packers did not open his practice window this week to begin his return. In Week 7, Green Bay plays the Detroit Lions before hosting the Panthers on “’Thursday Night Football’; believing Parsons needs more than a week to ramp up, the short-week turnaround would be difficult to pull off.” If this is truly the targeted return date, it would be realistic to see Parsons designated for return by Green Bay this week. This means he would be able to practice with the rest of the team, and the Packers would have 21 days to add him to the active roster. While he will not play in that many games in 2026, Green Bay is hopeful that his return will take their already impressive defense under Jonathan Gannon to an even higher level. The Green Bay Packers have lost several players to season-ending injuries already this year. These include defensive stars Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargrave as well as offensive stars Zach Tom and Jayden Reed. Despite these losses, and terrible play from their offensive line early in year, Green Bay has gone 3-2 in their first five games. Parsons, who was acquired prior to the start of the 2025 season in a trade with the Dallas Cowboys, tore his ACL in late in the year and has missed every game of 2026 thus far. Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported on Saturday morning that those around the NFL expect Parsons back in Week Nine when Green Bay faces the New England Patriots : Last season, Parsons became the first player in NFL history to record 12+ sacks in each of his first five seasons. He had 12.5 in 14 games played in his first season with the Packers and was named First Team All-Pro. home.blurb: Cowboys Injury Report: 2 Out, 4 Questionable vs. Packers Home FRISCO, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and offensive tackle Drew Shelton for Sunday night’s game at the Green Bay Packers , and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , defensive tackle L.T. Overton , and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on Friday’s final injury report. Durant and Shelton did not practice all week with hamstring injuries. Overshown was limited Thursday and Friday with his hamstring after missing Wednesday, and coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that he still considers Overshown a long shot. “Yeah, doing okay. Again, I still think it’s probably a long shot for this game, but it was good to see him out there moving around a little bit better,” Schottenheimer said. Porter appeared on the report with an ankle injury. He was limited Wednesday, a full participant Thursday, and limited again Friday. Porter missed last week’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with an illness, and defensive coordinator Christian Parker said Thursday that Porter’s workload would be heavily increased this week. Overton was added to the report Friday with a foot injury and did not practice. Speed was limited Thursday and Friday with a knee injury after missing Wednesday. Packers Rule Out Four, Including Javon Hargrave Green Bay ruled out defensive tackles Jonathan Ford and Javon Hargrave , receiver Skyy Moore , and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste . Defensive tackle Jordon Riley , who is in his 21-day return-to-practice window, is doubtful with an Achilles injury. Guard Aaron Banks is questionable with a knee and toe injury, along with defensive tackle Anthony Campbell with an ankle injury, cornerback Brandon Cisse with a hip injury added Friday, center/guard Jacob Monk with a quadriceps injury, and receiver Savion Williams , who has an ankle injury and is also in his return window. ‘I Just Kept Throwing Up’: Joey Porter Jr. Details Illness That Kept Him Out Against Buccaneers, Targets Green Bay A New Ankle Listing For Joey Porter Jr. Full Go For CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Smith, And Alijah Clark Safety Alijah Clark , who has been dealing with a hamstring injury, practiced fully all three days and carries no game status. So did left tackle Tyler Guyton with a back injury, outside linebacker James Houston with a shoulder injury, receiver CeeDee Lamb with a thigh injury, cornerback Shavon Revel with a knee injury, and left guard Tyler Smith with his surgically repaired thumb. Lamb said Thursday that his thigh bruise started in the second quarter of the Cowboys’ win at Houston and that he was back to square one after the mini-bye. Cornerback Keisean Nixon , edge rusher Lukas Van Ness , safety Evan Williams , and defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt carry no game status. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights San Francisco can improve to 6-0 and strengthen its NFC West lead, while Washington enters Levi's Stadium looking to pull off a sizable road upset Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Monday Night Football," the San Francisco 49ers play host to the Washington Commanders . San Francisco is riding high atop the NFC West with a 5-0 record, having defeated the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in a barnburner last week. The Niners have battled injuries on both sides of the ball all season, yet have remained unbeaten. They can create a three-game lead in the division with a victory on Monday night. Washington is coming off an absolute debacle last Sunday against the New York Giants , wherein the Commanders had a chance to kick a field goal to win the game at the end of overtime, but bungled the clock management as badly as any team you'll ever see. The Commies are just 1-3-1 entering this game, and they're looking to avoid falling further into the basement in the NFC East. Will the Niners continue to roll, or will the Commanders pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch 49ers vs. Commanders live Date: Monday, Oct. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: Levi's Stadium (Santa Clara, California) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: 49ers -7.5, O/U 52.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball Jayden Daniels looked no worse for wear last week in his return from another dislocated elbow. He completed 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards, while also rushing nine times for 103 yards and two touchdowns. Had he and the entire offense not totally brain-farted at the end of overtime, it would have been a wildly encouraging performance for Washington's rest-of-season outlook. While Daniels has been excellent when taking off to run in his three starts, Washington's running backs have been extremely inefficient on the ground. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (who was ruled out for this game after not practicing all week), Rachaad White , Austin Ekeler and the recently-released Kaytron Allen have combined to average just 3.7 yards per carry. The offensive line has created little push up front, with the backs collectively gaining just 0.95 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, and the backs themselves have broken tackles at the second-lowest rate in all of football. The 49ers, meanwhile, have allowed just 3.7 yards per rush to enemy running backs, with great tackling being the primary method of limiting yardage. Backs have gained 1.47 yards per carry before contact (an above-average mark), but only 2.22 yards after contact thanks to the lowest broken-tackle rate in the league. As a result, San Francisco has allowed only two explosive runs all season, per Tru Media, the fewest in the NFL . San Francisco has also been mostly strong against the pass, checking in 10th in opponents' EPA per dropback and 5th in opponents' success rate. The 49ers have allowed quarterbacks to complete only 64.4% of their passes at an average of 6.1 yards per attempt, with just five touchdowns and three interceptions in five games. It's tough to know what to make of Washington's passing game because it hasn't been at full strength for most of the season. Daniels missed two-and-a-half games. Chig Okonwko missed two. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs each missed one and saw their snaps limited in another. The Daniels-McLaurin-Diggs trio has shared the field for only 57 plays so far this season, according to Tru Media. Daniels is just 15 of 30 for 129 yards on those plays, but he has thrown for three scores and scrambled for 62 yards. Daniels should, in theory, see at least some clean pockets with the 49ers again playing without Nick Bosa , but Washington's offensive line has yielded pressure on over 38% of dropbacks so far this season, so the Niners could have a chance to get into Daniels' lap and force him into tough throws and mistakes. With the generally sticky coverage the San Francisco corners have played so far this season, it could be tough sledding for Washington in the passing game on Monday night. When the 49ers have the ball San Francisco has been the league's fourth-most efficient offense by EPA per play, according to Tru Media, ranking second with the pass and 14th with the run. Brock Purdy is playing at as high a level as any quarterback in football, completing 69% of his passes at an average of 8.4 yards per attempt with a league-high 13 touchdown passes and just two interceptions. Purdy also has a 57.9% passing success rate, which ranks as the best in the league. Purdy has done that despite hemorrhaging wide receivers throughout the season. Ricky Pearsall was lost for the year in training camp. Christian Kirk (listed as questionable for this week) has yet to make his 49er debut. De'Zhaun Stribling was injured in Week 1. Demarcus Robinson went down in Week 2. Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing were knocked out of last week's win over the Seahawks. Mike Evans has been playing through a painful rib injury. (He's also questionable for Monday night.) George Kittle spent the first two weeks ramping up to a full workload after last season's Achilles tear. And yet, here the 49ers are. Washington, meanwhile, has been one of the league's friendliest pass defenses. Every team the Commanders have faced has thrown for at least 257 net yards. Four of the five teams have gone more than 300 and two of them exceeded 400. The Commanders have allowed opponents to complete 65.2% of passes at an average of 7.1 yards per attempt, with 14 touchdowns and just three interceptions. The 103.9 passer rating against the Commanders to date is the sixth-worst mark in the league. It's very easy to see San Francisco finding success through the air so long as Evans suits up for the game. Christian McCaffrey is sharing the workload in the run game far more this season than in years past, with 61 carries for 286 yards againt Kaelon Black's 37 carries for 136 yards. McCaffrey's 4.7 yards-per-carry average is far better than what he posted over the last two years (4.0 and 3.9), and his rushing success rate of 45.9% is seventh-best out of 48 qualifying running backs. That figure is the second-best mark of his career, behind only the 2023 season, during which he led the NFL in rushing yards. The Commanders have actually been stingy against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry, with opposing backs limited to 0.69 yards per attempt before contact by the defensive front. Washington having similar success stopping the run here is important because it could make the 49ers one-dimensional, but the Commanders' pass-funnel defense also plays right into San Francisco's hands because of how efficient the 49ers' passing game has been so far this year. Purdy and Co. should eat, even if McCaffrey doesn't. I picked against the 49ers last week and regretted it almost immediately after seeing how their offense struggled against the stingy Seattle defense. Needless to say, Washington's defense is not of the same quality. I know the 49ers are still hemorrhaging wide receivers, but as long as Brock Purdy, Mike Evans, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey are healthy and Kyle Shanahan is calling the plays, they are going to move the ball efficiently. And I don't trust the Commanders to do quite enough to keep up with their explosive offense. The San Francisco 49ers and Brock Purdy are looking to keep their undefeated season going when they host the Washington Commanders and former No. 2 overall pick Jayden Daniels. San Francisco upset the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5, and it has one of the best offenses in the league during this perfect 5-0 start. Purdy is gaining some MVP buzz, and the 49ers have battled through several major injuries to sit atop the NFC standings. Meanwhile, Washington tied the New York Giants in Week 5 after a late-game blunder led to the clock expiring on the team – in field goal range – in overtime. Daniels and the Commanders are now just 1-3-1 this season (0-2-1 when Daniels plays), and they need as many wins as they can get to remain in the mix to win the NFC East. The 49ers are considerable favorites in this game, and the total is one of the highest of the week at 50.5. In the leadup to this game, the SI Betting team has made game picks, player props selections and much more to help bettors get the most out of this matchup. I’ve decided to compile some of our favorite plays all into one spot ahead of Monday’s action. Here’s a breakdown of each of these bets – and their latest odds in the Commanders vs. 49ers matchup. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Commanders vs. 49ers Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook San Francisco 49ers -7.5 (-110) vs. Washington Commanders – Iain MacMillan Brock Purdy OVER 2.5 Passing Touchdowns (+146) – Peter Dewey Jayden Daniels OVER 36.5 Rushing Yards (-109) – Peter Dewey Mike Evans Anytime TD (-140) – Peter Dewey All season long, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column . In Week 6, he’s taking the 49ers to cover at home: The only argument you can make to bet on the Commanders in this game, and it's not necessarily one that I'd disagree with, is that so many things have gone right for the 49ers through the first five weeks that they're bound to have a game where things go wrong. If that happens, and if Jayden Daniels can drag the Commanders' offense down the field enough, maybe Washington can cover this spread. With that being said, that's not enough for me to take the Commanders here, and considering I expect the line to shift even more towards San Francisco this week, I'll take them at -7.5 while I still can. There's a strong argument to be made that the 49ers are the best team in the NFL. They're second in net yards per play (+1.7), second in EPA per play, first in success rate, fourth in opponent EPA per play, and eighth in opponent success rate. They're well-balanced on both sides of the ball, and now they get to host a bad Commanders team in a prime time slot. There's a chance this game gets ugly. Brock Purdy has thrown at least two scores in every game this season, and he has two games with three or more touchdown passes (against the Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals). Washington has given up the most touchdown passes in the league (14) through five weeks, and Jameis Winston torched this secondary in the second half of Week 5. Overall, the Commanders are 23rd in EPA/Pass and 29th in passing yards allowed in 2026. This is a dream matchup for Purdy, who has thrown the ball just over 28 times per game for the offense that is No. 1 in success rate and No. 2 in EPA/Play this season. At +146, I think this prop is worth a shot against one of the worst pass defenses in the NFL. Jayden Daniels has only played in three games this season, but the Commanders quarterback has 203 rushing yards and two scores. Now, 103 of those yards came in Week 5 against the New York Giants, but Daniels has cleared this rushing yards total twice, picking up over 60 yards in two of his games. The 49ers’ defense is a top-five unit in EPA/Rush, so I expect plenty of dropbacks for Daniels on Monday night. Since the star quarterback has such a unique rushing ability, I wouldn’t be shocked if he escapes the pocket a few times for long scrambles. After all, Daniels has at least five carries in every game this season, including nine in his return from a dislocated elbow. If I’m betting on Purdy to throw three scores, I might as well take Mike Evans to catch one! Evans has three touchdown catches in the 2026 season, reeling in a season-high seven passes for 113 yards and a score in Week 5. Evans remains one of the best red zone threats in the NFL because of his size, turning six targets into five receptions and two scores inside the opponent’s 20-yard-line. Purdy has thrown multiple touchdowns in every game this season (13 overall), and the Washington defense is tied for the most passing scores allowed (14) in 2026. The Commanders are also just 23rd in the NFL in EPA/Pass. This isn’t the best price, but Evans should have a few chances to find the end zone in Week 6. The San Francisco 49ers and Brock Purdy have been an exciting offense to follow all season long, as they’re 5-0 and have scored the third-most points in the league. Veterans like Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle give the 49ers a ton of firepower on offense, and they could be a tough team for the Washington Commanders to handle. Washington has a 1-3-1 record in 2026 and is set as a 7.5-point underdog in this primetime matchup. While Jayden Daniels helped this offense improve from a disastrous Week 4 showing, the Washington defense ranks in the bottom-10 in the league in both success rate and EPA/Play. The betting market has taken notice, and oddsmakers are expecting a high-scoring game on Monday night. The total for this matchup is up at 50.5 with the OVER (-120) heavily favored. Purdy and the 49ers have the No. 2 offense in EPA/Play and the No. 3 offense in yards per play this season, so Washington’s defense will have its hands full on Monday night. On the other side, Daniels clearly raises the ceiling of Washington’s attack, and he had two rushing scores in his first game back from his dislocated elbow. There are a ton of great playmakers to bet on to find the end zone on Monday night, but I’ve narrowed things down to my top three for Commanders vs. 49ers. Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Commanders vs. 49ers Odds via FanDuel Sportsbook Mike Evans Anytime TD (-140) Mike Evans has three touchdown catches in the 2026 season, reeling in a season-high seven passes for 113 yards and a score in Week 5. Evans remains one of the best red zone threats in the NFL because of his size, turning six targets into five receptions and two scores inside the opponent’s 20-yard-line. Brock Purdy has thrown multiple touchdowns in every game this season (13 overall), and the Washington defense is tied for the most passing scores allowed (14) in 2026. The Commanders are also just 23rd in the NFL in EPA/Pass. This isn’t the best price, but Evans should have a few chances to find the end zone in Week 6. Terry McLaurin Anytime TD (+170) Terry McLaurin missed Week 4 with a hamstring issue, but he played over 58 percent of Washington’s snaps in Week 5, catching all four of his targets for 62 yards. Daniels being back in the lineup boosts this entire offense, and is worth noting that McLaurin scored in Week 3 with Marcus Mariota under center, a sign that he was starting to heat up in 2026. The star wideout should get a ton of work against a San Fran defense that is worse against the pass (13th in EPA/Pass) than the run (fifth in EPA/Rush). With Stefon Diggs (hamstring banged up), McLaurin should lead the Washington passing game on Monday. Jayden Daniels Anytime TD (+260) In his return from a dislocated elbow against the New York Giants, Daniels carried the ball nine times for 103 yards, finding the end zone twice. He’s a serious threat as a rusher, and I wouldn’t be shocked if he takes off quite a bit against a San Francisco defense that has the sixth-best pressure rate in the NFL in 2026. Frankly, I’m surprised Daniels is pushing 3/1 to score since he’s found the end zone 10 times on the ground in just 27 NFL appearances. San Francisco may have a tough time containing the former No. 2 overall pick, as he’s ran for over 30 yards in every game he’s played in this season. If McLaurin is out for a significant time, as expected, Stefon Diggs is going to have to show why he’s one of the premier wideouts in the game to support the passing game. Alongside Diggs, this injury will open up more opportunities for rookie WR Antonio Williams to flourish. But their bad injury luck continued as star wide receiver Terry McLaurin went down with an apparent knee injury and was carted off the field. away.headline: 49ers sputter in second half after Mike Evans' injury but hold on to beat Commanders to improve to 6-0
away.blurb: For now, San Francisco's perfect season rolls on. The 49ers raced out to a 20-point lead and it looked like they would cruise to an easy win over the Washington Commanders. But San Francisco's offense stalled with No. 1 receiver Mike Evans sidelined with an Achilles injury he suffered late in the first half, allowing the Commanders to get back in the game. The Niners' defense, which has been a big surprise all season, came up with two big stops in the final two minutes to seal the 23-17 win. The 49ers improved to 6-0 to start the season. It wouldn't be a 49ers game without a key injury. Evans, who came into the game with injuries to his ribs and Achilles tendon, left Monday night's game due to the Achilles. He stayed down after a catch late in the second quarter and went straight to the locker room with athletic trainers. He was ruled out of the game by the team. Washington wasn't finished. It forced a three-and-out and got the ball back with less than a minute to go, but no timeouts. A fair catch interference call helped with field position. The Commanders were running out of time but a 17-yard catch by rookie receiver Antonio Williams got the ball to San Francisco's 28-yard line. But an intentional grounding penalty on Daniels was a crushing blow, especially since there was a 10-second runoff, leaving only six seconds on the clock. A sack on the final play sealed the win. away.headline: Washington Commanders Star Wide Receiver Terry McLaurin Carted Off With Potentially Significant Knee Injury
away.blurb: The knee injury represents McLaurin's second health issue of the current campaign. He previously sat out Washington's October 4 loss against the Indianapolis Colts in London due to a hamstring strain before returning the following week to haul in four passes for 62 yards in a tie against the New York Giants. The 31-year-old receiver is currently navigating his eighth NFL season, having spent his entire professional career with Washington after being selected in the third round of the 2019 NFL Draft out of Ohio State. Across 112 career regular-season games—all as a starter—he has posted 513 receptions for 7,191 yards and 42 touchdowns. Washington will return to prime-time action on November 1, when they host the Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) in a pivotal divisional matchup. If McLaurin is forced to miss extended time, Washington's coaching staff will need to restructure their offensive system around the remaining receiving corps. Washington Commanders star wide receiver Terry McLaurin suffered a serious setback on Monday night, leaving the field on a medical cart during the team's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Santa Clara, California. Head coach Dan Quinn expressed immediate concern following the contest, confirming that the left knee injury "could be significant" and acknowledging widespread fear within the organization that upcoming medical evaluation will reveal a major ailment. The injury occurred late in the first quarter with minimal contact, dealing a devastating blow to Washington's offensive unit. With the Commanders sitting at 1-4-1 entering their bye week, the franchise anxiously awaits diagnostic results on its star wideout before returning to action on November 1. Non-Contact Injury Forces McLaurin Off in Air Cast The troubling scene unfolded late in the opening quarter while McLaurin was running a pass route toward the sideline. Covered closely by San Francisco defender Deommodore Lenoir, the veteran wide receiver went down under minimal physical contact and immediately grabbed at his left knee in visible distress. Medical staff rushed onto the field to evaluate the 31-year-old playmaker as teammates gathered around. Personnel fitted McLaurin's left leg with a protective air cast before helping him onto the cart to be driven off the field for further evaluation in the locker room. away.headline: How long is Terry McLaurin out? Latest updates on Commanders WR's knee injury
away.blurb: McLaurin was injured in the first quarter and did not return. Now, it looks like he'll miss significant time as a result. Here's everything to know about McLaurin's knee injury and how long he will be out for the Commanders. How long is Terry McLaurin out? The Commanders quickly ruled out McLaurin with a knee injury . That said, Washington's bigger loss was its star wide receiver, Terry McLaurin , who was carted off with a knee injury . The veteran receiver has already missed one game this year while dealing with a hamstring injury in Week 4. According to the latest reports on Tuesday, Oct. 20, it's possible McLaurin's latest injury is far more severe. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said after the "Monday Night Football" game that the team is concerned McLaurin's injury "could be significant." The veteran wideout will undergo more scans on Tuesday, Oct. 20, Quinn said. Further updates will come when the head coach speaks to the media later in the day on Oct. 20. NFL Media and ESPN insider Ian Rapoport reported the morning of Oct. 20 that McLaurin "is feared to have suffered a serious and season-ending knee injury." What happened to Terry McLaurin? McLaurin was carted off the field during the Commanders' Week 6 "Monday Night Football" game after suffering a knee injury in the first quarter. The injury appeared to be non-contact while he was running a route. He got up and walked to the cart with some assistance. His left leg was put in an air cast before teammates surrounded him as he left the game. Below is a full look at the play that injured McLaurin. The team made the decision shortly after the receiver was carted off the field in the first quarter on "Monday Night Football" against the 49ers. The Commanders did not provide an official status update after the game, but head coach Dan Quinn said the star receiver will undergo further testing. "The concern is that it could be significant," Quinn said after the game. "We'll do the scans tomorrow and give you an update." Alongside Diggs, this injury will open up more opportunities for rookie WR Antonio Williams to flourish. home.headline: 49ers sputter in second half after Mike Evans' injury but hold on to beat Commanders to improve to 6-0
home.blurb: For now, San Francisco's perfect season rolls on. The 49ers raced out to a 20-point lead and it looked like they would cruise to an easy win over the Washington Commanders. But San Francisco's offense stalled with No. 1 receiver Mike Evans sidelined with an Achilles injury he suffered late in the first half, allowing the Commanders to get back in the game. The Niners' defense, which has been a big surprise all season, came up with two big stops in the final two minutes to seal the 23-17 win. The 49ers improved to 6-0 to start the season. It wouldn't be a 49ers game without a key injury. Evans, who came into the game with injuries to his ribs and Achilles tendon, left Monday night's game due to the Achilles. He stayed down after a catch late in the second quarter and went straight to the locker room with athletic trainers. He was ruled out of the game by the team. Washington wasn't finished. It forced a three-and-out and got the ball back with less than a minute to go, but no timeouts. A fair catch interference call helped with field position. The Commanders were running out of time but a 17-yard catch by rookie receiver Antonio Williams got the ball to San Francisco's 28-yard line. But an intentional grounding penalty on Daniels was a crushing blow, especially since there was a 10-second runoff, leaving only six seconds on the clock. A sack on the final play sealed the win. home.headline: 49ers week 6 injury report vs. Commanders: WRs to target in fantasy football with Mike Evans banged up
home.blurb: Head coach Kyle Shanahan is doing anything but breathing easy at this point. The 49ers have suffered a slew of injuries that have impacted them throughout the season, and there is no let up as they prepare for the Commanders. They have gotten a dynamic performance from the QB-RB-WR trio of Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and Mike Evans to this point in the season, but Evans is battered and bruised in his first season with the 49ers. He is listed as questionable for the Week 6 Monday night game. He has been battling bruised ribs and now he also has an Achilles issue that kept him out of practice Friday. It would be a major blow if the 49ers did not have him in the lineup against the Commanders. While Shanahan and Purdy have to be prepared for that possibility and have alternatives in mind, Evans will fight to remain in the lineup. “We all know what he’s been playing through, the immense pain that he has every single play,” said 49ers center Jake Brendel , per Matt Barrows of The Athletic . “He still goes out there and does his very best to get a completion for us. It’s fantastic.” Brandin Cooks will be the Niners’ primary deep threat in this game, and if Evans can’t play or is severely limited, he will become their No. 1 receiver. Cooks has only played in 2 games this season and his numbers are not significant. He has caught just 3-7-1, but that does not mean he would struggle in this game. Cooks is a 13-year veteran receiver with the tools and the know-how to make a key contribution. The San Francisco 49ers (5-0) have been the most impressive team in the NFL as they prepare for their Week 6 Monday night game against the Washington Commanders. Perhaps apologies are due to the Minnesota Vikings (5-0) and the Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) as the only other undefeated teams in the NFL. But perhaps not. The Niners have had much more difficult assignments than the Chiefs and they have had a much stronger offense than the Vikings. Evans was one of the best receivers with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for 12 years and he regularly played through injuries and showed up on an every-game basis for the first 11 years of his career. He was held to 8 games last year with the Bucs after suffering a broken collarbone that required surgery. Evans is a warrior and will play vs. Commanders Evans has been everything the Niners hoped he would be when they signed him as a free agent in the offseason. The former Tampa Bay star smelled a potential Super Bowl opportunity with his new team and he has played like it. Evans leads the 49ers with 24 receptions for 326 yards and 3 TDs. While he is no longer at the peak of his athletic ability, his know-how on the field makes him one of the most dangerous receivers when it comes to making plays that keep drives alive. home.blurb: However, star wide receiver Mike Evans got off to a fast start with three receptions for 94 yards in the second quarter before aggravating his Achilles injury, which kept him out of practice all week. Fortunately, the 49ers play the Atlanta Falcons this week before heading into their bye. Christian Kirk also appears to be getting close to a return, which would help San Francisco's offense. Concerning Truth About Mike Evans’ Injury Emerges After 49ers Win Unlock the latest Heavy on 49ers news — direct to your inbox. Updated Oct 20, 2026 at 12:42pm The San Francisco 49ers secured a 23-17 victory over the Washington Commanders on Monday night to improve to 6-0 on the season. Concerning Truth Emerges About Evans' Injury After the game, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans may miss some time but confirmed that he hadn't suffered a tear and that the injury wasn't overly serious. On Tuesday, NFL Network's Mike Garafolo provided more insight into Evans' injury, revealing a concerning detail the wide receiver may have to manage moving forward, especially if he doesn't miss any games. "A lot of times when you see a team report an Achilles injury you go oh no. But not in this case. This is an Achilles injury that is not a tear but it something that Mike Evans has dealt with and will continue to have to deal with," Garafolo reported. "Mike Evans at this point in his career plays such a physical style of wide receiver… and if its a question of pain tolerance. This is the kind of guy that'll battle through it," he added. "But he's got an Achilles issue that Kyle Shanahan said after the game something that he's had before and it was bothering him throughout the week and he's hopeful he'll be able to play in the teams next game."
